title.zh: 卷三百二十二 列傳第二百一十 外國三 日本
title.raw: 卷三百二十二 列傳第二百一十 外國三 日本 Volume 322 Biographies 210: Foreign States 3: Japan

sentences.zh: 日本，古倭奴國。

translations.literal: Japan is the ancient Wo-nu state.
translations.idiomatic: Japan was formerly known as the land of Wo.

sentences.zh: 唐咸亨初，改日本，以近東海日出而名也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianheng era of Tang, it was changed to Japan, named because it lies near the Eastern Sea where the sun rises.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xianheng period of the Tang dynasty, the name was changed to Japan, so called because the country lies near the Eastern Sea where the sun rises.

sentences.zh: 地環海，惟東北限大山，有五畿、七道、三島，共一百十五州，統五百八十七郡。

translations.literal: The land is encircled by the sea, bounded only in the northeast by great mountains; it has five kinai circuits, seven roads, and three islands, altogether one hundred fifteen provinces governing five hundred eighty-seven districts.
translations.idiomatic: The country is surrounded by sea, with great mountains marking its northeastern frontier. It is divided into the five capital circuits, seven roads, and three islands, comprising one hundred fifteen provinces and five hundred eighty-seven districts in all.

sentences.zh: 其小國數十，皆服屬焉。

translations.literal: Several tens of small states all submit and are attached to it.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of lesser states all acknowledge its authority.

sentences.zh: 國小者百里，大不過五百里。

translations.literal: The small states are a hundred li; the large do not exceed five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The smallest domains measure a hundred li across; the largest scarcely reach five hundred.

sentences.zh: 戶小者千，多不過一二萬。

translations.literal: Households in the small are a thousand; for the most part they do not exceed ten or twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The least populous have a thousand households; most have no more than ten or twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 國主世以王為姓，群臣亦世官。

translations.literal: The rulers of the state take Wang as their surname by hereditary succession; the ministers also hold office by hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house bears the surname Wang by hereditary succession, and ministerial offices are likewise hereditary.

sentences.zh: 宋以前皆通中國，朝貢不絕，事具前史。

translations.literal: Before the Song all had intercourse with China, tribute missions never ceasing; the matters are fully recorded in previous histories.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Song dynasty Japan maintained continuous contact with China through tribute missions, as detailed in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 惟元世祖數遣使趙良弼招之不至，乃命忻都、範文虎等帥舟師十萬征之，至五龍山遭暴風，軍盡沒。

translations.literal: Only Emperor Shizu of Yuan repeatedly sent the envoy Zhao Liangbi to summon them but they did not come; then he ordered Xin Du, Fan Wenhu, and others to lead a fleet of one hundred thousand to attack them; at Wulong Mountain they encountered a violent storm and the army was entirely lost.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan, Kublai Khan repeatedly sent Zhao Liangbi to summon Japan to submit, but the Japanese refused. He then ordered Xin Du, Fan Wenhu, and others to lead a fleet of one hundred thousand men against them; at Mount Wulong a violent storm struck, and the entire force perished.

sentences.zh: 後屢招不至，終元世未相通也。

translations.literal: Later they were repeatedly summoned but did not come; through the entire Yuan age there was no intercourse.
translations.idiomatic: Further summons went unanswered, and throughout the Yuan dynasty the two countries had no diplomatic contact.

sentences.zh: 明興，高皇帝即位，方國珍、張士誠相繼誅服。

translations.literal: When the Ming arose, the founding emperor took the throne; Fang Guozhen and Zhang Shicheng were successively executed and subdued.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming dynasty was founded and the Hongwu Emperor took the throne, Fang Guozhen and Zhang Shicheng were defeated in turn.

sentences.zh: 諸豪亡命，往往糾島人入寇山東濱海州縣。

translations.literal: Various powerful men in flight often gathered islanders to raid the coastal prefectures and counties of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Dispossessed warlords often rallied Japanese islanders to raid the coastal prefectures and counties of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年三月，帝遣行人楊載詔諭其國，且詰以入寇之故，謂：「宜朝則來廷，不則修兵自固。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Hongwu, the emperor sent the emissary Yang Zai with an edict to instruct their state, and also questioned them on the reason for raiding, saying: If you wish to pay court, then come to the audience; if not, then prepare your troops and secure your own defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Hongwu year 2, the emperor sent the emissary Yang Zai with an edict to Japan, demanding an explanation for the raids. He declared: If you wish to submit, come to court; if not, strengthen your defenses.

sentences.zh: 倘必為寇盜，即命將徂征耳，王其圖之。」

translations.literal: If you must be raiders and bandits, then I shall at once order generals to march against you—Your Majesty, consider this.
translations.idiomatic: If you persist in piracy, I shall send generals to campaign against you. Your Majesty, weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 日本王良懷不奉命，復寇山東，轉掠溫、台、明州旁海民，遂寇福建沿海郡。

translations.literal: The king of Japan, Liang Huai, did not obey the command; he again raided Shandong, turned to plunder the coastal people near Wen, Tai, and Ming prefectures, and then raided the coastal commanderies of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese king Ashikaga did not obey. He raided Shandong again, then turned to plunder coastal communities near Wenzhou, Taizhou, and Mingzhou, and finally attacked the coastal prefectures of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 三年三月又遣萊州府同知趙秩責讓之，泛海至析木崖，入其境，守關者拒弗納。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year he again sent Zhao Zhi, associate prefect of Laizhou, to rebuke them; crossing the sea he reached Ximu Cliff, entered their territory, and the border guards refused and would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 3 the court again sent Zhao Zhi, associate prefect of Laizhou, to rebuke Japan. He sailed to Ximu Cliff and entered Japanese territory, but border guards refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 秩以書抵良懷，良懷延秩入。

translations.literal: Zhi sent a letter to reach Liang Huai; Liang Huai invited Zhi in.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhi sent a letter to Ashikaga, who then received him.

sentences.zh: 諭以中國威德，而詔書有責其不臣語。

translations.literal: He instructed them on the majesty and virtue of China, while the edict contained words rebuking their failure to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhi expounded on the majesty and virtue of China, while the edict rebuked Japan for refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 良懷曰：「吾國雖處扶桑東，未嘗不慕中國。

translations.literal: Liang Huai said: Although our state lies east of Fusang, we have never failed to admire China.
translations.idiomatic: Ashikaga replied: Though our country lies east of Fusang, we have always admired China.

sentences.zh: 惟蒙古與我等夷，乃欲臣妾我。

translations.literal: Only the Mongols, who are barbarians like us, wished to make us their subjects and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: But the Mongols are barbarians like us, yet they sought to reduce us to vassalage.

sentences.zh: 我先王不服，乃使其臣趙姓者訹我以好語，語未既，水軍十萬列海岸矣。

translations.literal: Our former king would not submit; then they sent their minister surnamed Zhao to entice me with fair words—before the words were finished, a naval force of one hundred thousand was arrayed along the coast.
translations.idiomatic: Our former king refused to submit. They sent a minister named Zhao to lure us with fair words, but before he had finished speaking, a fleet of one hundred thousand men lined our shores.

sentences.zh: 以天之靈，雷霆波濤，一時軍盡覆。

translations.literal: By Heaven's numinous power, thunder, waves, and billows—at once the army was entirely overturned.
translations.idiomatic: By Heaven's grace, thunder and towering waves destroyed the entire army at once.

sentences.zh: 今新天子帝中夏，天使亦趙姓，豈蒙古裔耶？

translations.literal: Now the new Son of Heaven rules central Xia, and the heavenly envoy is also surnamed Zhao—can he be of Mongol descent?
translations.idiomatic: Now a new Son of Heaven reigns over China, and your envoy is also surnamed Zhao—are you Mongols as well?

sentences.zh: 亦將訹我以好語而襲我也。」

translations.literal: Will you also entice me with fair words and then attack me?
translations.idiomatic: Will you likewise entice us with fair words and then strike?

sentences.zh: 自左右將兵之。

translations.literal: He himself drew his attendants to marshal troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered his attendants to summon troops.

sentences.zh: 秩不為動，徐曰：「我大明天子神聖文武，非蒙古比，我亦非蒙古使者後。

translations.literal: Zhi was unmoved and said slowly: Our Great Ming Son of Heaven is divine, sagely, civil, and martial—no comparison to the Mongols; I am also not a successor of the Mongol envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhi remained unmoved and replied calmly: The Son of Heaven of Great Ming is divine, sagely, civil, and martial—nothing like the Mongols. Nor am I any successor to their envoys.

sentences.zh: 能兵，兵我。」

translations.literal: If you can fight, then fight me.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to fight, then make war on us.

sentences.zh: 良懷氣沮，下堂延秩，禮遇甚優。

translations.literal: Liang Huai's spirit was discouraged; he came down from the hall to receive Zhi and treated him with very generous courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Ashikaga's defiance collapsed. He came down from the hall to receive Zhao Zhi and treated him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 遣其僧祖來奉表稱臣，貢馬及方物，且送還明、台二郡被掠人口七十餘，以四年十月至京。

translations.literal: He sent his monk Zulai to present a memorial declaring himself subject, tribute horses and local products, and also returned more than seventy persons plundered from Ming and Tai prefectures; they reached the capital in the tenth month of the fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the monk Zulai with a memorial submitting as a vassal, tribute horses and local products, and returned more than seventy captives taken from Mingzhou and Taizhou. The embassy reached the capital in the tenth month of year 4.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，宴賚其使者，念其俗佞佛，可以西方教誘之也，乃命僧祖闡、克勤等八人送使者還國，賜良懷《大統歷》及文綺、紗羅。

translations.literal: The founding emperor commended this, feasted and rewarded their envoys; considering their custom of worshiping Buddha, they could be enticed by the Western teaching—thereupon he ordered the monks Zuchan, Keqin, and seven others to escort the envoys back to their state, and bestowed on Liang Huai the Datong Calendar and patterned silks, gauze, and damask.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor commended this and feasted the envoys. Reflecting that the Japanese were devoted to Buddhism and might be won over through religion, he sent eight monks including Zuchan and Keqin to escort the embassy home, and granted Ashikaga the Datong Calendar along with brocades, gauzes, and silks.

sentences.zh: 是年掠溫州。

translations.literal: That year they raided Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Japanese raiders attacked Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年寇海鹽、澉浦，又寇福建海上諸郡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year they raided Haiyan and Ganpu, and again raided the maritime commanderies of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 they raided Haiyan and Ganpu, then struck the coastal prefectures of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 六年以於顯為總兵官，出海巡倭，倭寇萊、登。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Yu Xian was made commander-in-chief to patrol the Wo at sea; the Wo raided Lai and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 Yu Xian was appointed commander-in-chief to patrol the coast against Japanese pirates, but the Japanese nonetheless raided Laizhou and Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖闡等既至，為其國演教， 其國人頗敬信。

translations.literal: When Zuchan and the others arrived, they expounded the teaching in that state, and its people were quite respectful and believing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuchan and his companions arrived, they preached in Japan, and the people received the teaching with considerable respect.

sentences.zh: 而王則傲慢無禮，拘之二年，以七年五月還京。

translations.literal: But the king was arrogant and without propriety, detained them for two years, and in the fifth month of the seventh year they returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The king, however, was arrogant and discourteous, and detained them for two years before they returned to the capital in the fifth month of year 7.

sentences.zh: 倭寇膠州。

translations.literal: The Wo raided Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese raiders attacked Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 時良懷年少，有持明者，與之爭立，國內亂。

translations.literal: At that time Liang Huai was young; there were those who upheld the Ming cause who contended with him for the throne, and the state was in internal disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Ashikaga was then young, and rivals who supported the Southern Court contested the succession, throwing the country into civil strife.

sentences.zh: 是年七月，其大臣遣僧宣聞溪等齎書上中書省，貢馬及方物，而無表。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year his great ministers sent the monks Xuanwenxi and others bearing a letter to the Secretariat, tribute horses and local products, but no memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year his ministers sent the monks Xuanwenxi and others with a letter to the Secretariat, horses and local products as tribute, but no formal memorial of submission.

sentences.zh: 帝命卻之，仍賜其使者遣還。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered it refused, yet still rewarded their envoys and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the tribute refused but still bestowed gifts on the envoys and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其別島守臣氏久遣僧奉表來貢。

translations.literal: Before long, the guarding minister of another island, Uji, sent monks presenting a memorial to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Uji, a guardian official of another island, sent monks with a memorial offering tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝以無國王之命，且不奉正朔，亦卻之，而賜其使者，命禮臣移牒，責以越分私貢之非。

translations.literal: The emperor, because there was no royal command and they did not observe the correct calendar, also refused it, yet rewarded their envoys and ordered the ritual officials to send a dispatch rebuking the impropriety of overstepping rank with private tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Because the mission lacked the king's authorization and did not observe the Chinese calendar, the emperor refused this tribute as well, though he still rewarded the envoys. The Ministry of Rites was ordered to send a dispatch rebuking the impropriety of unauthorized private tribute.

sentences.zh: 又以頻入寇掠，命中書移牒責之。

translations.literal: Also because of frequent raids and plunder, he ordered the Secretariat to send a dispatch rebuking them.
translations.idiomatic: Because of repeated raids, the Secretariat was also ordered to send a dispatch of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 乃以九年四月，遣僧圭廷用等來貢，且謝罪。

translations.literal: Then in the fourth month of the ninth year they sent the monks Guitingyong and others to come with tribute and also to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 9 they sent the monks Guitingyong and others with tribute and an apology.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其表詞不誠，降詔戒諭，宴賚使者如制。

translations.literal: The emperor disliked the insincerity of the wording of their memorial, issued an edict of admonition and instruction, and feasted and rewarded the envoys according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found the memorial insincere and issued an edict of admonition, but still feasted and rewarded the envoys according to protocol.

sentences.zh: 十二年來貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year they came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 十三年復貢，無表，但持其征夷將軍源義滿奉丞相書，書辭又倨。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year they again sent tribute, without a memorial, only bearing a letter from their barbarian-quelling general Minamoto Yoshimitsu presented to the chief minister; the wording of the letter was again arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 they sent tribute again without a memorial, presenting only a letter from the shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu to the chief minister—and its tone was again arrogant.

sentences.zh: 乃卻其貢，遣使齎詔譙讓。

translations.literal: Thereupon their tribute was refused, and envoys were sent bearing an edict of rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused the tribute and sent envoys with an edict of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 十四年復來貢，帝再卻之，命禮官移書責其王，並責其征夷將軍，示以欲征之意。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year they again came with tribute; the emperor again refused it and ordered the ritual officials to send a letter rebuking their king and also rebuking their barbarian-quelling general, showing the intention to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 they sent tribute once more. The emperor refused it again and ordered the Ministry of Rites to rebuke both the king and the shogun, making clear his intent to launch a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 良懷上言：臣聞三皇立極，五帝禪宗，惟中華之有主，豈夷狄而無君。

translations.literal: Liang Huai submitted a statement: Your subject has heard that the Three Sovereigns established the pole, the Five Emperors transmitted the regalia—only central Hua has a lord; how could the barbarians and Di have no rulers?
translations.idiomatic: Ashikaga submitted a memorial: I have heard that the Three Sovereigns established order and the Five Emperors passed down the regalia. China has its sovereign—but are we barbarians without rulers of our own?

sentences.zh: 乾坤浩蕩，非一主 之獨權，宇宙寬洪，作諸邦以分守。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth are vast and boundless—not the sole authority of one lord; the cosmos is wide and ample, making the various states to divide and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth are vast; sovereignty is not the monopoly of a single ruler. The cosmos is wide, and many realms were made to govern their own domains.

sentences.zh: 蓋天下者，乃天下之天下，非一人之天下也。

translations.literal: For All-under-Heaven is the All-under-Heaven of the world—not the All-under-Heaven of one man.
translations.idiomatic: All-under-Heaven belongs to all the world—not to one man alone.

sentences.zh: 臣居遠弱之倭，褊小之國，城池不滿六十，封疆不足三千，尚存知足之心。

translations.literal: Your subject dwells in distant, weak Wo, a narrow, small state—city walls not reaching sixty, frontiers not reaching three thousand—yet still preserves a heart of knowing sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: I dwell in distant, feeble Japan, a small and narrow realm with fewer than sixty walled towns and a frontier of less than three thousand li—yet I am content with what I have.

sentences.zh: 陛下作中華之主，為萬乘之君，城池數千餘，封疆百萬里，猶有不足之心，常起滅絕之意。

translations.literal: Your Majesty acts as lord of central Hua, as ruler of ten thousand chariots—city walls numbering several thousands, frontiers of a million li—yet still has a heart of insufficiency and constantly raises thoughts of annihilation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reigns as sovereign of China, lord of ten thousand chariots, with thousands of walled cities and a frontier of a million li—yet you are never satisfied and constantly harbor designs to destroy us.

sentences.zh: 夫天發殺機，移星換宿。

translations.literal: When Heaven releases the mechanism of killing, stars shift and lodges change.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven unleashes the engines of destruction, the stars shift and constellations change.

sentences.zh: 地發殺機，龍蛇走陸。

translations.literal: When earth releases the mechanism of killing, dragons and serpents run upon the land.
translations.idiomatic: When earth unleashes the engines of destruction, dragons and serpents course over the land.

sentences.zh: 人發殺機，天地反覆。

translations.literal: When man releases the mechanism of killing, heaven and earth overturn.
translations.idiomatic: When man unleashes the engines of destruction, heaven and earth are overturned.

sentences.zh: 昔堯、舜有德，四海來賓。

translations.literal: Formerly Yao and Shun had virtue, and the four seas came as guests.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Yao and Shun ruled with virtue, and the four seas came as guests.

sentences.zh: 湯、武施仁，八方奉貢。

translations.literal: Tang and Wu practiced benevolence, and the eight directions presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Wu practiced benevolence, and the eight directions offered tribute.

sentences.zh: 臣聞天朝有興戰之策，小邦亦有禦敵之圖。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the celestial court has policies for raising war, and small states also have plans for repelling the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the celestial court has strategies for waging war—but small states too have plans for defense.

sentences.zh: 論文有孔、孟道德之文章，論武有孫、吳韜略之兵法。

translations.literal: In literature there are the moral writings of Confucius and Mencius; in warfare there are the strategic military methods of Sun and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In letters you have the moral writings of Confucius and Mencius; in warfare you have the strategic arts of Sunzi and Wuzi.

sentences.zh: 又聞陛下選股肱之將，起精銳之師，來侵臣境。

translations.literal: I have also heard that Your Majesty selects pillar ministers as generals, raises elite troops, and comes to invade your subject's territory.
translations.idiomatic: I hear also that Your Majesty has chosen your finest generals and raised elite troops to invade my realm.

sentences.zh: 水澤之地，山海之洲，自有其備，豈肯跪途而奉之乎？

translations.literal: Lands of marshes and waters, islets of mountains and seas—have their own preparations; how could they kneel on the road and submit?
translations.idiomatic: Our watery marshes and mountain isles have defenses of their own. Would we kneel in the road and submit?

sentences.zh: 順之未必其生，逆之未必其死。

translations.literal: To submit does not necessarily mean living; to resist does not necessarily mean dying.
translations.idiomatic: Submission does not guarantee survival, nor does resistance guarantee death.

sentences.zh: 相逢賀蘭山前，聊以博戲，臣何懼哉。

translations.literal: Let us meet before Helan Mountain and for a time play at gaming—what has your subject to fear?
translations.idiomatic: Let us meet before Mount Helan and settle this as a contest of arms—what have I to fear?

sentences.zh: 倘君勝臣負，且滿上國之意。

translations.literal: If the lord wins and the subject loses, that will satisfy the superior state's intent.
translations.idiomatic: If you prevail and I am defeated, that will satisfy the celestial court.

sentences.zh: 設臣勝君負，反作小邦之差。

translations.literal: If your subject wins and the lord loses, that would instead be the disgrace of a small state.
translations.idiomatic: If I prevail and you are defeated, that would be the disgrace of a great power humbled by a small state.

sentences.zh: 自古講和為上，罷戰為強，免生靈之塗炭，拯黎庶之艱辛。

translations.literal: From antiquity negotiating peace has been supreme, ceasing war has been strength—sparing the people from being trampled in charcoal, rescuing the common folk from hardship.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity peace has been held supreme and ending war the mark of strength, sparing the people from slaughter and relieving the common folk from suffering.

sentences.zh: 特遣使臣，敬叩丹陛，惟上國圖之。

translations.literal: I specially send envoys respectfully to knock at the cinnabar steps—may the superior state consider this.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore send envoys to bow before your throne and ask that the celestial court give this matter your consideration.

sentences.zh: 帝得表慍甚，終鑑蒙古之轍，不加兵也。

translations.literal: The emperor, receiving the memorial, was very angry, but in the end took warning from the Mongol precedent and did not add troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious when he received the memorial, but reflecting on the Mongol precedent, he ultimately refrained from sending troops.

sentences.zh: 十六年，倭寇金鄉、平陽。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the Wo raided Jinxiang and Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 Japanese raiders attacked Jinxiang and Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 十九年遣使來貢，卻之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year they sent envoys to come with tribute; it was refused.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 they sent tribute envoys, but the court refused them.

sentences.zh: 明年命江夏侯周德興往福建濱海四郡，相視形勢。

translations.literal: The next year he ordered Marquis Jiangxia Zhou Dexing to go to the four coastal commanderies of Fujian to inspect the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he ordered Marquis Jiangxia Zhou Dexing to survey the terrain of Fujian's four coastal commanderies.

sentences.zh: 衛所城不當要害者移置之，民戶三丁取一，以充戍卒，乃築城一十六，增巡檢司四十五，得卒萬五千餘人。

translations.literal: Guard and battalion cities not at strategic points were relocated; from civilian households one man in three was taken to fill garrison troops—then sixteen cities were built, forty-five inspection offices added, obtaining more than fifteen thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Guard posts not sited at strategic points were relocated. One man in every three households was levied for coastal defense. Sixteen walled posts were built, forty-five inspection offices added, and more than fifteen thousand garrison troops raised.

sentences.zh: 又命信國公湯和行視浙東、西諸郡，整飭海防，乃築城五十九。

translations.literal: He also ordered Duke Xinguo Tang He to tour the eastern and western commanderies of Zhe, rectify coastal defense, and built fifty-nine cities.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Duke Xinguo Tang He to inspect the eastern and western prefectures of Zhejiang and reorganize coastal defenses, building fifty-nine fortified posts.

sentences.zh: 民戶四丁以上者以一為戍卒，得五萬八千七百餘人，分戍諸衛，海防大飭。

translations.literal: From households of four males or more, one was taken as a garrison soldier, obtaining fifty-eight thousand seven hundred-odd men, distributed to garrison the various guards—coastal defense was greatly rectified.
translations.idiomatic: From households with four adult males or more, one was conscripted, yielding fifty-eight thousand seven hundred men distributed among the coastal guards. Coastal defenses were thoroughly reorganized.

sentences.zh: 閏六月命福建備海舟百艘，廣東倍之，以九月會浙江捕倭，既而不行。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month he ordered Fujian to prepare one hundred seagoing vessels, Guangdong double that number, to assemble in Zhejiang in the ninth month to capture the Wo—but in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month he ordered Fujian to prepare one hundred seagoing vessels and Guangdong twice that number, to join Zhejiang in a ninth-month campaign against Japanese pirates—but the plan was never executed.

sentences.zh: 先是，胡惟庸謀逆，欲藉日本為助。

translations.literal: Previously, Hu Weiyong plotted rebellion and wished to borrow Japan as assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hu Weiyong had plotted rebellion and sought Japanese support.

sentences.zh: 乃厚結寧波衛指揮林賢，佯奏賢罪，謫居日本，令交通其君臣。

translations.literal: Then he greatly befriended Lin Xian, commander of Ningbo Guard, falsely memorialized Xian's crime, banished him to dwell in Japan, and ordered him to communicate with their ruler and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated ties with Lin Xian, commander of the Ningbo Guard, then falsely accused him and banished him to Japan to negotiate with the Japanese court.

sentences.zh: 尋奏復賢職，遣使召之，密緻書其王，借兵助己。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized to restore Xian's office, sent envoys to summon him, and secretly sent a letter to their king to borrow troops to assist himself.
translations.idiomatic: He soon had Lin Xian restored to office and recalled him, while secretly sending the Japanese king a letter requesting military aid.

sentences.zh: 賢還，其王遣僧如瑤率兵卒四百餘人，詐稱入貢，且獻巨燭，藏火藥、刀劍其中。

translations.literal: When Xian returned, their king sent the monk Ruyao leading more than four hundred soldiers and troops, falsely claiming to enter with tribute, and also presenting huge candles in which gunpowder, swords, and blades were hidden.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Xian returned, the Japanese king sent the monk Ruyao with more than four hundred armed men, pretending to offer tribute. They brought enormous candles concealing gunpowder, swords, and blades.

sentences.zh: 既至，而惟庸已敗，計不行。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Weiyong had already been defeated and the plan could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they arrived, Hu Weiyong had already been overthrown and the plot failed.

sentences.zh: 帝亦未知其狡謀也。

translations.literal: The emperor also did not yet know their crafty plot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still unaware of the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 越數年，其事始露，乃族賢，而怒日本特甚，決意絕之，專以防海為務。

translations.literal: After several years the matter came to light; then he exterminated Xian's clan, and was especially angry at Japan, resolved to break with them, and devoted himself solely to coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the plot was exposed. Lin Xian's entire clan was executed, and the emperor's wrath toward Japan was especially fierce. He resolved to sever relations and devoted himself entirely to coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 然其時王子滕祐壽者，來入國學，帝猶善待之。

translations.literal: Yet at that time the prince Teng Youshou came to enter the National University, and the emperor still treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, however, the Japanese prince Teng Youshou entered the Imperial University, and the emperor still treated him kindly.

sentences.zh: 二十四年五月特授觀察使，留之京師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-fourth year he was specially appointed observation commissioner and kept in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 24 he was specially appointed Observation Commissioner and retained at court.

sentences.zh: 後著《祖訓》，列不征之國十五，日本與焉。

translations.literal: Later, in composing the Ancestral Injunctions, he listed fifteen states not to be attacked, and Japan was among them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in the Ancestral Injunctions, he listed fifteen countries that were not to be attacked, and Japan was among them.

sentences.zh: 自是，朝貢不至，而海上之警亦漸息。

translations.literal: From this time tribute missions did not come, yet the alarms on the sea also gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute missions ceased, and coastal alarms gradually subsided.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，遣使以登極詔諭其國。

translations.literal: When Chengzu took the throne, he sent envoys with an accession edict to instruct their state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he sent envoys with an accession edict to Japan.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年又遣左通政趙居任、行人張洪偕僧道成往。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle he again sent the left bureau commissioner Zhao Juren, the emissary Zhang Hong, together with the monk Daocheng to go.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 he again sent Left Bureau Commissioner Zhao Juren, Emissary Zhang Hong, and the monk Daocheng.

sentences.zh: 將行，而其貢使已達寧波。

translations.literal: When they were about to depart, their tribute envoys had already reached Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could depart, Japanese tribute envoys had already reached Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 禮官李至剛奏：「故事，番使入中國，不得私攜兵器鬻民。

translations.literal: The ritual official Li Zhigang memorialized: By precedent, when barbarian envoys enter China they must not privately carry weapons and sell them to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Li Zhigang memorialized: By precedent, foreign envoys entering China may not privately carry weapons to sell to the populace.

sentences.zh: 宜敕所司核其舶，諸犯禁者悉籍送京師。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the responsible offices to inspect their ships; all who violate the prohibition should be entirely registered and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices should be ordered to inspect their vessels, and all contraband seized and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「外夷修貢，履險蹈危，來遠，所費實多。

translations.literal: The emperor said: When outer barbarians present tribute, they tread danger and risk, coming from afar—the expense is truly great.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: Foreign peoples undertaking tribute missions brave great perils traveling from afar, at considerable expense.

sentences.zh: 有所齎以助資斧，亦人情，豈可概拘以禁令。

translations.literal: To have something brought to assist their travel expenses is also human feeling—how can they all be bound by prohibitions?
translations.idiomatic: It is only natural that they bring goods to defray their expenses. They cannot all be bound by rigid prohibitions.

sentences.zh: 至其兵器，亦準時直市之，毋阻向化。」

translations.literal: As for their weapons, they should also be purchased at current fair value, and must not obstruct their turning toward civilization.
translations.idiomatic: As for their weapons, let them be purchased at fair market price, and do not obstruct those who seek to submit.

sentences.zh: 十月，使者至，上王源道義表及貢物。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the envoys arrived, presenting the memorial of King Minamoto Michiyoshi and tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the envoys arrived, presenting a memorial from King Ashikaga Michiyoshi along with tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 帝厚禮之，遣官偕其使還，賚道義冠服、龜鈕金章及錦綺、紗羅。

translations.literal: The emperor treated them with generous courtesy, sent officials to accompany their envoys back, and bestowed on Michiyoshi court dress, a gold seal with tortoise knob, and brocades, gauzes, and damasks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received them with great honor, sent officials to escort the embassy home, and granted Michiyoshi court robes, a gold seal with tortoise knob, and brocades, gauzes, and silks.

sentences.zh: 明年十一月來賀冊立皇太子。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the next year they came to congratulate the investiture of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the eleventh month, they came to congratulate the investiture of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時對馬、台岐諸島賊掠濱海居民，因諭其王捕之。

translations.literal: At that time the islands of Tsushima, Taqi, and others had bandits plundering coastal residents; therefore he instructed their king to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time pirates from Tsushima, Tashima, and other islands were raiding coastal communities, and the emperor instructed the Japanese king to capture them.

sentences.zh: 王發兵盡殲其眾，縶其魁二十人，以三年十一月獻於朝，且修貢。

translations.literal: The king sent troops and entirely annihilated their bands, bound twenty of their leaders, and in the eleventh month of the third year presented them at court, and also renewed tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent troops who exterminated the pirates, captured twenty of their leaders, and presented them at court in the eleventh month of year 3, while also renewing tributary relations.

sentences.zh: 帝益嘉之，遣鴻臚寺少卿潘賜偕中官王進賜其王九章冕服及錢鈔、錦綺加等，而還其所獻之人，令其國自治之。

translations.literal: The emperor was all the more pleased, and dispatched Pan Ci, Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, together with the eunuch Wang Jin to bestow upon the king the ceremonial robes of nine emblems, as well as paper money, brocades, and silks of enhanced grade; and he returned the persons they had presented, ordering their own country to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased. He sent Vice Minister Pan Ci of the Court of State Ceremonial and the eunuch Wang Jin to grant the king ceremonial robes bearing the nine insignia of rank, along with paper money, brocades, and silks of the highest grade. He also returned the captives they had presented, instructing Japan to deal with them under its own laws.

sentences.zh: 使者至寧波，盡置其人於甑，烝殺之。

translations.literal: When the envoys reached Ningbo, they placed all of those persons in steamers and steamed them to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys reached Ningbo, they placed every one of the captives in steamers and steamed them alive.

sentences.zh: 明年正月又遣侍郎俞士吉齎璽書褒嘉，賜賚優渥。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Vice Minister Yu Shiji was again dispatched carrying an imperial sealed edict of commendation, and generous gifts were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the first month, Vice Minister Yu Shiji was sent again with a sealed imperial letter of praise, and lavish gifts were granted.

sentences.zh: 封其國之山為壽安鎮國之山，御製碑文，立其上。

translations.literal: A mountain in their country was enfeoffed as the Mountain of Longevity and Tranquility that Guards the State; the emperor personally composed an inscription and had it erected upon the summit.
translations.idiomatic: A mountain in Japan was enfeoffed as Mount Shou'an, Guardian of the Realm. The emperor composed an inscription in his own hand and had it erected on the peak.

sentences.zh: 六月，使來謝，賜冕服。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, envoys came to offer thanks, and ceremonial robes were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, envoys arrived to express gratitude, and ceremonial robes were granted.

sentences.zh: 五年、六年頻入貢，且獻所獲海寇。

translations.literal: In the fifth and sixth years they frequently sent tribute, and moreover presented the sea bandits they had captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth and sixth years they sent tribute repeatedly and also presented the sea pirates they had captured.

sentences.zh: 使還，請賜仁孝皇后所制《勸善》、《內訓》二書，即命各給百本。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned, they requested the two works composed by Empress Renxiao, Exhortation to Goodness and Inner Admonitions; the emperor immediately ordered a hundred copies of each to be given.
translations.idiomatic: On their return, the envoys asked for the two books composed by Empress Renxiao, Exhortation to Goodness and Inner Admonitions. The emperor at once ordered a hundred copies of each to be provided.

sentences.zh: 十一月再貢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month they sent tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they presented tribute once more.

sentences.zh: 十二月，其國世子源義持遣使來告父喪，命中官周全往祭，賜謚恭獻，且致賻。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Minamoto Yoshimochi, heir to the throne, dispatched envoys to announce his father's death; the emperor ordered the eunuch Zhou Quan to go perform the mourning rites, conferred the posthumous title Gongxian, and also sent condolence gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, the heir Yoshimochi sent envoys to announce his father's death. The emperor ordered the eunuch Zhou Quan to perform the mourning rites, granted the late king the posthumous title Gongxian, and sent funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 又遣官齎敕，封義持為日本國王。

translations.literal: Officials were again dispatched carrying an imperial edict to enfeoff Yoshimochi as King of Japan.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were again sent with an imperial edict investing Yoshimochi as King of Japan.

sentences.zh: 時海上復以倭警告，再遣官諭義持剿捕。

translations.literal: At that time warnings of Wo raids again came from the sea, and officials were again dispatched to instruct Yoshimochi to suppress and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time fresh warnings of Japanese piracy arrived from the coast, and the court again sent officials instructing Yoshimochi to hunt the raiders down.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，義持遣使謝恩，尋獻所獲海寇，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, Yoshimochi dispatched envoys to express gratitude; shortly thereafter he presented captured sea bandits, and the emperor commended this.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year, Yoshimochi sent envoys to give thanks. Soon afterward he presented captured sea pirates, and the emperor praised the gesture.

sentences.zh: 明年二月復遣王進齎敕褒賚，收市物貨。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, Wang Jin was again dispatched carrying an imperial edict with commendations and gifts, and to purchase goods in trade.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the second month, Wang Jin was sent again with an imperial edict bearing praise and gifts, and to purchase trade goods.

sentences.zh: 其君臣謀阻進不使歸，進潛登舶，從他道遁還。

translations.literal: The king and his ministers plotted to detain Jin and prevent his return; Jin secretly boarded a ship and escaped back by another route.
translations.idiomatic: The king and his ministers plotted to hold Jin back and keep him from returning. Jin secretly boarded a ship and fled home by another route.

sentences.zh: 自是，久不貢。

translations.literal: From this time forth, for a long while they did not send tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After that, Japan sent no tribute for many years.

sentences.zh: 是年，倭寇盤石。

translations.literal: That year, Wo bandits raided Panshi.
translations.idiomatic: That year Japanese pirates attacked Panshi.

sentences.zh: 十五年，倭寇松門、金鄉、平陽。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Wo bandits raided Songmen, Jinxiang, and Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Japanese pirates raided Songmen, Jinxiang, and Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 有捕倭寇數十人至京者。

translations.literal: There were some who captured several tens of Wo bandits and brought them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Some officials captured several dozen Japanese pirates and brought them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 廷臣請正法。

translations.literal: Court officials requested that they be punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials asked that the captives be punished under the law.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「威之以刑，不若懷之以德，宜還之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "To awe them with punishments is not as good as winning them with virtue; they should be sent back."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "It is better to win them with kindness than to overawe them with punishment. They should be sent back."

sentences.zh: 乃命刑部員外郎呂淵等齎敕責讓，令悔罪自新。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Vice Minister of Justice Lü Yuan and others to carry an imperial edict rebuking and reproaching them, ordering them to repent and reform.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Vice Minister of Justice Lü Yuan and others to carry an imperial edict of rebuke, commanding the pirates to repent and reform.

sentences.zh: 中華人被掠者，亦令送還。

translations.literal: Chinese persons who had been abducted were also ordered to be sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese subjects who had been abducted were also to be returned.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，其王遣使隨淵等來貢，謂：「海寇旁午，故貢使不能上達。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year, the king dispatched envoys to come present tribute together with Yuan and the others, stating: "Sea bandits come thick and fast, and therefore tribute envoys cannot reach Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the fourth month, the king sent envoys to present tribute alongside Lü Yuan's party, explaining: "Sea pirates swarm everywhere, so tribute missions cannot reach Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 其無賴鼠竊者，實非臣所知。

translations.literal: Those worthless petty thieves are truly not known to this subject.
translations.idiomatic: As for those worthless petty thieves, I truly know nothing of them.

sentences.zh: 願貸罪，容其朝貢。」

translations.literal: I beg that my crimes be pardoned and that tribute missions be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: I beg forgiveness for my offenses and ask that tribute missions be allowed to resume."

sentences.zh: 帝以其詞順，許之，禮使者如故，然海寇猶不絕。

translations.literal: The emperor, because his words were compliant, assented; the envoys were treated with ritual as before, yet sea bandits still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding the reply conciliatory, agreed. The envoys were received with the usual ceremony, but piracy on the seas did not stop.

sentences.zh: 十七年，倭船入王家山島，都督劉榮率精兵疾馳入望海堝。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Wo ships entered Wangjiashan island; Regional Commander Liu Rong led crack troops racing swiftly to Wanghaigang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Japanese ships entered Wangjiashan Island. Regional Commander Liu Rong led elite troops in a forced march to Wanghaigang.

sentences.zh: 賊數千人分乘二十舟，直抵馬雄島，進圍望海堝。

translations.literal: Several thousand bandits in twenty boats went straight to Maxiong island and advanced to besiege Wanghaigang.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand raiders in twenty boats made straight for Maxiong Island and then pressed on to besiege Wanghaigang.

sentences.zh: 榮發伏出戰，奇兵斷其歸路。

translations.literal: Rong deployed ambush troops and went out to battle; surprise forces cut off their line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sprung his ambush and gave battle; a flanking force cut off the enemy's retreat.

sentences.zh: 賊奔櫻桃園，榮合兵攻之，斬首七百四十二，生擒八百五十七。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Cherry Orchard; Rong combined his forces and attacked them, beheading seven hundred forty-two and capturing eight hundred fifty-seven alive.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders fled to Cherry Orchard. Rong united his forces and attacked, beheading seven hundred forty-two men and taking eight hundred fifty-seven alive.

sentences.zh: 召榮至京，封廣寧伯。

translations.literal: Rong was summoned to the capital and enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was summoned to court and enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangning.

sentences.zh: 自是，倭不敢窺遼東。

translations.literal: From this time, the Wo dared not cast their eyes upon Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: After that, the Japanese pirates no longer dared threaten Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 二十年，倭寇象山。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Wo bandits raided Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, Japanese pirates raided Xiangshan.

sentences.zh: 宣德七年正月，帝念四方蕃國皆來朝，獨日本久不貢，命中官柴山往琉球，令其王轉諭日本，賜之敕。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year of the Xuande reign, the emperor, reflecting that foreign countries from all quarters had come to court while Japan alone had long sent no tribute, ordered the eunuch Chai Shan to go to Ryukyu and have its king relay instructions to Japan, bestowing upon them an imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year of Xuande, the emperor noted that tributary states from every direction had come to court while Japan alone had long stayed away. He ordered the eunuch Chai Shan to go to Ryukyu and have its king convey a message to Japan, along with an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，王源義教遣使來。

translations.literal: In the summer of the following year, King Ashikaga Yoshinori dispatched envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer, King Ashikaga Yoshinori sent envoys.

sentences.zh: 帝報之，賚白金、彩幣。

translations.literal: The emperor responded, bestowing white silver and colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with gifts of silver and colored silks.

sentences.zh: 秋復至。

translations.literal: In the autumn they came again.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn they came again.

sentences.zh: 十年十月以英宗嗣位，遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year, upon the succession of Emperor Yingzong, they dispatched envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the tenth year, when Emperor Yingzong succeeded to the throne, they sent envoys to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年入貢，至臨清，掠居民貨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Jingtai reign they sent tribute; when they reached Linqing, they plundered the goods of residents.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingtai they sent tribute, but on reaching Linqing they looted local residents' goods.

sentences.zh: 有指揮往詰，歐幾死。

translations.literal: A military commander went to interrogate them and was nearly beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: A commander went to question them and was nearly beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 所司請執治，帝恐失遠人心，不許。

translations.literal: The responsible offices requested that they be arrested and punished, but the emperor, fearing loss of the hearts of distant peoples, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities asked to arrest and punish them, but the emperor, fearing he would lose the goodwill of distant peoples, refused.

sentences.zh: 先是，永樂初，詔日本十年一貢，人止二百，船止二艘，不得攜軍器，違者以寇論。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the beginning of the Yongle reign, an edict had decreed that Japan should send tribute once every ten years, with no more than two hundred persons and two ships, and that they must not carry military weapons; violators were to be treated as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the start of Yongle, an edict had fixed tribute from Japan at once every ten years, with no more than two hundred men and two ships, and forbade the carrying of weapons. Violators were to be treated as pirates.

sentences.zh: 乃賜以二舟，為入貢用，後悉不如制。

translations.literal: Thereupon two boats were bestowed for use in presenting tribute, but afterward they all fell short of the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Two vessels were then granted for tribute missions, but afterward the Japanese consistently violated the rules.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，申定要約，人毋過三百，舟毋過三艘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xuande reign, the essential terms were reaffirmed: persons must not exceed three hundred, boats must not exceed three.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xuande the terms were tightened again: no more than three hundred persons and three ships.

sentences.zh: 而倭人貪利，貢物外所攜私物增十倍，例當給直。

translations.literal: Yet the Japanese, greedy for profit, brought private goods beyond tribute tenfold the amount, which by precedent required fair payment.
translations.idiomatic: But the Japanese, greedy for profit, carried private merchandise ten times the volume of tribute goods, all of which by precedent had to be purchased at fair price.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「宣德間所貢硫黃、蘇木、刀扇、漆器之屬，估時直給錢鈔，或折支布帛，為數無多，然已大獲利。

translations.literal: The ritual officials said: "During the Xuande period the tribute of sulfur, sappanwood, swords and fans, lacquerware and the like was appraised at current value and paid in paper money, or disbursed in cloth and silk; the amounts were not large, yet they already reaped great profit.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites reported: "During Xuande, tribute items such as sulfur, sappanwood, swords, fans, and lacquerware were appraised at market value and paid in paper money or cloth and silk. The sums were modest, yet the Japanese already made enormous profit.

sentences.zh: 今若仍舊制，當給錢二十一萬七千，銀價如之。

translations.literal: If we now follow the old regulations, we should pay two hundred seventeen thousand in cash, with silver at equivalent value.
translations.idiomatic: If we now pay according to the old scale, the amount would be two hundred seventeen thousand in cash, with silver at equivalent value.

sentences.zh: 宜大減其直，給銀三萬四千七百有奇。」

translations.literal: The fair price should be greatly reduced, paying thirty-four thousand seven hundred-odd taels of silver."
translations.idiomatic: The price should be sharply reduced, to a little over thirty-four thousand seven hundred taels of silver."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 使臣不悅，請如舊制。

translations.literal: The envoy was displeased and requested payment according to the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was displeased and asked that the old rate be restored.

sentences.zh: 詔增錢萬，猶以為少，求增賜物。

translations.literal: An edict added ten thousand in cash, yet he still thought it too little and requested additional gifts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added ten thousand in cash, but he still considered it insufficient and asked for more gifts.

sentences.zh: 詔增布帛千五百，終怏怏去。

translations.literal: An edict added one thousand five hundred in cloth and silk; he departed still discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict added fifteen hundred units of cloth and silk. He left still resentful.

sentences.zh: 天順初，其王源義政以前使臣獲罪天朝，蒙恩宥，欲遣使謝罪而不敢自達，移書朝鮮王令轉請，朝鮮以聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianshun reign, King Ashikaga Yoshimasa, because previous envoys had been guilty before the Celestial Court yet had been pardoned in grace, wished to dispatch envoys to express regret but did not dare do so directly; he sent a letter to the King of Korea asking him to intercede, and Korea reported this.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianshun, King Ashikaga Yoshimasa, whose earlier envoys had offended the Ming court but been pardoned, wished to send a mission of apology but did not dare approach directly. He wrote to the King of Korea asking him to intercede, and Korea relayed the request.

sentences.zh: 廷議敕朝鮮核實，令擇老成識大體者充使，不得仍前肆擾，既而貢使亦不至。

translations.literal: The court deliberated and issued an edict to Korea to verify the facts and to choose persons of mature character who grasped the larger principles to serve as envoys, who must not again behave as before with unrestrained harassment; yet tribute envoys still did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The court deliberated and ordered Korea to verify the facts and to choose sober, responsible men as envoys who would not repeat their earlier misconduct. Even so, no tribute mission came.

sentences.zh: 成化四年夏，乃遣使貢馬謝恩，禮之如制。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year of the Chenghua reign, envoys were finally dispatched to present horses in gratitude; they were treated with ritual according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year of Chenghua, envoys finally arrived with horses to express gratitude. They were received according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 其通事三人，自言本寧波村民，幼為賊掠，市與日本，今請便道省祭，許之。

translations.literal: Three of their interpreters stated that they were originally villagers of Ningbo, abducted as children by bandits and sold to Japan; they now requested permission to return home by a convenient route to pay respects at family graves, which was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Three interpreters said they were originally villagers from Ningbo, kidnapped as children by pirates and sold in Japan. They asked permission to visit home by a convenient route to tend family graves, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 戒其勿同使臣至家，引中國人下海。

translations.literal: They were warned not to bring envoys to their homes or lead Chinese people to go to sea.
translations.idiomatic: They were warned not to bring the envoys to their homes or induce Chinese subjects to go to sea.

sentences.zh: 十一月，使臣清啟復來貢，傷人於市。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the envoy Kiyohiro came again with tribute and wounded people in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the envoy Kiyohiro came again with tribute and injured people in the market.

sentences.zh: 有司請治其罪，詔付清啟，奏言犯法者當用本國之刑，容還國如法論治。

translations.literal: The local offices requested that he be punished; an edict handed the matter to Kiyohiro, who memorialized that offenders should be punished by their own country's laws, requesting that they be allowed to return home for lawful adjudication.
translations.idiomatic: Local authorities asked that he be punished. An edict referred the matter to Kiyohiro, who replied that offenders should be judged under Japanese law and asked that they be allowed to return home for trial.

sentences.zh: 且自服不能鈐束之罪，帝俱赦之。

translations.literal: He also personally acknowledged the crime of failing to restrain them; the emperor pardoned all.
translations.idiomatic: He also confessed his own failure to restrain his men. The emperor pardoned everyone involved.

sentences.zh: 自是，使者益無忌。

translations.literal: From this time, envoys grew all the more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: After that, the envoys grew ever bolder.

sentences.zh: 十三年九月來貢，求《佛祖統紀》諸書，詔以《法苑珠林》賜之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year they came with tribute, requesting the Buddhist texts Universal Chronicle of the Buddha and others; an edict granted them Pearl Forest of the Dharma Garden.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year they came with tribute and asked for Buddhist works including the Universal Chronicle of the Buddha. An edict granted them the Pearl Forest of the Dharma Garden instead.

sentences.zh: 使者述其王意，請於常例外增賜，命賜錢五萬貫。

translations.literal: The envoy relayed his king's intention, requesting an additional grant beyond the usual allotment; an order was issued granting fifty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy conveyed his king's wish for extra gifts beyond the usual allowance, and an order was issued granting fifty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 二十年十一月復貢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twentieth year they sent tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the twentieth year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年三月，王源義高遣使來，還至濟寧，其下復持刀殺人。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year of the Hongzhi reign, King Ashikaga Yoshihisa dispatched envoys; when returning they reached Jining, and his subordinates again drew swords and killed people.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the ninth year of Hongzhi, King Ashikaga Yoshihisa sent envoys. On the return journey, when they reached Jining, his subordinates again drew swords and killed people.

sentences.zh: 所司請罪之，詔自今止許五十人入都，余留舟 次，嚴防禁焉。

translations.literal: The responsible offices requested that they be punished; an edict decreed that henceforth only fifty persons would be permitted to enter the capital, the rest to remain aboard ship, with strict prohibitions enforced.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities asked that they be punished. An edict ruled that henceforth only fifty men might enter the capital; the rest were to remain aboard ship under strict guard.

sentences.zh: 十八年冬來貢，時武宗已即位，命如故事，鑄金牌勘合給之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighteenth year they came with tribute; as Emperor Wuzong had already ascended the throne, they were ordered treated according to precedent, and a gold tally plate of verification was cast and given them.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eighteenth year they came with tribute. Emperor Wuzong had already ascended the throne, so they were received according to precedent and a gold tally of verification was cast and granted.

sentences.zh: 正德四年冬來貢。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of the Zhengde reign they came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year of Zhengde they came with tribute.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「明年正月，大祀慶成宴。

translations.literal: The ritual officials said: "In the first month of next year, after the great sacrifice there will be the celebration banquet.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites reported: "In the first month of next year, after the great sacrifice there will be the celebratory banquet.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮陪臣在展東第七班，日本向無例，請殿西第七班。」

translations.literal: Korean attendant ministers are in the seventh rank on the east side of the hall extension; Japan has had no precedent; request the seventh rank on the west side of the hall."
translations.idiomatic: Korean envoys sit in the seventh rank on the east side of the extended hall. Japan has no established place. We ask that they be assigned the seventh rank on the west side."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 禮官又言：「日本貢物向用舟三，今止一，所賜銀幣，宜如其舟之數。

translations.literal: The ritual officials also said: "Japan's tribute goods have customarily used three boats; now there is only one; the silver and silks granted should correspond to the number of boats.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites also reported: "Japan's tribute missions have customarily used three ships; this time there is only one. The silver and silks granted should match the number of ships.

sentences.zh: 且無表文，賜敕與否，請上裁。」

translations.literal: Moreover there is no memorial; whether to grant an imperial edict or not — request the emperor's decision."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, they have brought no memorial. Whether to grant an imperial edict is for Your Majesty to decide."

sentences.zh: 命所司移文答之。

translations.literal: An order was issued for the responsible offices to reply by official dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: An order was issued for the relevant offices to reply by official dispatch.

sentences.zh: 五年春，其王源義澄遣使臣宋素卿來貢，時劉瑾竊柄，納其黃金千兩，賜飛魚服，前所未有也。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, King Ashikaga Yoshizumi dispatched the envoy Song Suqing to present tribute; at that time Liu Jin held power in secret, accepted a thousand taels of gold from him, and bestowed flying-fish robes — something without precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year, King Ashikaga Yoshizumi sent the envoy Song Suqing with tribute. Liu Jin was then wielding power behind the throne; he accepted a thousand taels of gold from Suqing and granted him flying-fish robes — an honor without precedent.

sentences.zh: 素卿，鄞縣硃氏子，名縞，幼習歌唱。

translations.literal: Suqing was a son of the Zhu family of Yin County, named Gao; in youth he studied singing.
translations.idiomatic: Suqing was a son of the Zhu family of Yin County, born Gao. In youth he trained in song and dance.

sentences.zh: 倭使見，悅之，而縞叔澄負其直，因以縞償。

translations.literal: When the Wo envoys saw him they were pleased; but Gao's uncle Cheng owed them money, so Gao was given in payment.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese envoys took a liking to him, but Gao's uncle Cheng owed them money, so Gao was handed over to settle the debt.

sentences.zh: 至是，充正使，至蘇州，澄與相見。

translations.literal: At this time he served as chief envoy; when he reached Suzhou, Cheng met with him.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had become chief envoy. When he reached Suzhou, Cheng came to see him.

sentences.zh: 後事覺，法當死，劉瑾庇之，謂澄已自首，並獲免。

translations.literal: When the matter later came to light, by law he deserved death; Liu Jin shielded him, saying Cheng had already surrendered himself, and both were granted pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair later came to light, the law called for his death. Liu Jin protected him, claiming Cheng had already surrendered, and both men were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 七年，義澄使復來貢，浙江守臣言：「今畿輔、山東盜充斥，恐使臣遇之為所掠，請以貢物貯浙江官庫，收其表文送京師。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Yoshizumi's envoys came again with tribute; Zhejiang frontier officials said: "Now bandits fill the capital region and Shandong; we fear the envoys may encounter them and be plundered; request that tribute goods be stored in the official warehouses of Zhejiang and their memorial be sent to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Yoshizumi's envoys came again with tribute. Zhejiang officials reported: "Bandits now fill the capital region and Shandong. We fear the envoys may be robbed on the road. We ask that tribute goods be stored in Zhejiang's official warehouses and the memorial sent on to the capital."

sentences.zh: 禮官會兵部議，請令南京守備官即所在宴賚，遣歸，附進方物，皆予全直，毋阻遠人向化心。

translations.literal: The ritual officials met with the Ministry of War to deliberate; they requested that the Nanjing garrison commander immediately at their location entertain and grant gifts and send them back, with attached tribute goods all paid full value, and not obstruct the distant people's desire to turn toward civilization.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites and the Ministry of War jointly recommended that the Nanjing garrison commander entertain and reward the envoys on the spot and send them home, paying full value for all attached goods and not discouraging distant peoples from submitting.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The recommendation was approved.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年五月，其貢使宗設抵寧波。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of the Jiajing reign, their tribute envoy Sōsetsu reached Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Jiajing, the tribute envoy Sōsetsu reached Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 未幾，素卿偕瑞佐復至，互爭真偽。

translations.literal: Before long, Suqing arrived together with Mizuo, and they contended over which was genuine.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Suqing arrived with Mizuo, and the two parties disputed which mission was authentic.

sentences.zh: 素卿賄市舶大監賴恩，宴時坐素卿於宗設上，船後至又先為驗發。

translations.literal: Suqing bribed the maritime trade superintendent eunuch Lai En; at the banquet Suqing was seated above Sōsetsu, and though his boat arrived later it was first inspected and cleared for trade.
translations.idiomatic: Suqing bribed the maritime trade eunuch Lai En. At the banquet Suqing was seated above Sōsetsu, and though his ship arrived later it was inspected and cleared first.

sentences.zh: 宗設怒，與之斗，殺瑞佐，焚其舟，追素卿至紹興城下，素卿竄匿他所免。

translations.literal: Sōsetsu was enraged and fought with him, killing Mizuo, burning their boat, and pursuing Suqing to below Shaoxing city; Suqing hid elsewhere and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Sōsetsu flew into a rage and fought him, killing Mizuo, burning their ship, and chasing Suqing to the walls of Shaoxing. Suqing hid elsewhere and escaped.

sentences.zh: 凶黨還寧波，所過焚掠，執指揮袁璡，奪船出海。

translations.literal: The violent party returned to Ningbo, burning and plundering all along the way, seized Commander Yuan Jin, and took boats to go out to sea.
translations.idiomatic: The violent faction returned to Ningbo, burning and looting as they went, seized Commander Yuan Jin, and took ships out to sea.

sentences.zh: 都指揮劉錦追至海上，戰沒。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Liu Jin pursued them to sea and was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Liu Jin pursued them to sea and was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史歐珠以聞，且言：「據素卿狀，西海路多羅氏義興者，向屬日本統轄，無入貢例。

translations.literal: Censor Ouyang Zhu reported this, and furthermore said: "According to Suqing's account, one Yixing of the Tara clan of the Western Sea Route had long been under Japanese jurisdiction and had no precedent for sending tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ouyang Zhu reported the affair and added: "According to Suqing, a man named Yixing of the Tara clan on the Western Sea route had long been under Japanese control and had no right to send tribute.

sentences.zh: 因貢道必經西海，正德朝勘合為所奪。

translations.literal: Because the tribute route must pass through the Western Sea, the tally plates of the Zhengde reign were seized by them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the tribute route had to pass through the Western Sea, the Zhengde tally plates were seized.

sentences.zh: 我不得已，以弘治朝勘合，由南海路起程，比至寧波，因詰其偽，致啟釁。」

translations.literal: We had no choice but to take the Hongzhi tally plates and set out by the Southern Sea Route; when we reached Ningbo, because they challenged our authenticity, conflict arose.
translations.idiomatic: We had no choice but to use the Hongzhi tally plates and sail by the Southern Sea route. When we reached Ningbo and were challenged as impostors, violence broke out.

sentences.zh: 章下禮部，部議：「素卿言未可信，不宜聽入朝。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the Ministry of Rites; the ministry deliberated: "Suqing's words cannot be trusted; he should not be permitted to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Ministry of Rites, which ruled: "Suqing's account cannot be trusted; he should not be allowed to enter court.

sentences.zh: 但釁起宗設，素卿之黨被殺者多，其前雖有投番罪，已經先朝宥赦，毋容問。

translations.literal: But the provocation originated with Sōsetsu; many of Suqing's followers were killed; though he earlier had the crime of going over to foreign tribes, he had already been pardoned by the previous reign — he must not be held accountable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the provocation began with Sōsetsu, and many of Suqing's men were killed. Though Suqing had once committed the crime of going over to the Japanese, he had already been pardoned in the previous reign and should not be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 惟宣諭素卿還國，移咨其王，令察勘合有無，行究治。」

translations.literal: Only instruct Suqing to return to his country and send a dispatch to his king, ordering investigation into whether tally plates exist and proper punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Simply order Suqing to return home and send a dispatch to his king instructing him to verify the tally plates and punish those responsible."

sentences.zh: 帝已報可，御史熊蘭、給事張翀交章言：「素卿罪重不可貸，請並治賴恩及海道副使張芹、分守參政硃鳴陽、分巡副使許完、都指揮張浩。

translations.literal: The emperor had already approved, when Censor Xiong Lan and Submitter Zhang Chong jointly memorialized: "Suqing's crimes are grave and cannot be pardoned; request also punishment for Lai En, Deputy Commissioner of the Maritime Circuit Zhang Qin, Regional Vice Commissioner Zhu Mingyang, Circuit Vice Commissioner Xu Wan, and Regional Commander Zhang Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already approved when Censor Xiong Lan and Submitter Zhang Chong jointly memorialized: "Suqing's crimes are too grave to pardon. We ask that Lai En, Maritime Deputy Commissioner Zhang Qin, Regional Vice Commissioner Zhu Mingyang, Circuit Vice Commissioner Xu Wan, and Regional Commander Zhang Hao also be punished.

sentences.zh: 閉關絕貢，振中國之威，寢狡寇之計。」

translations.literal: Close the borders and cut off tribute, displaying China's authority, and thwarting the schemes of crafty raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Close the borders, cut off tribute, assert the dignity of the empire, and frustrate the designs of cunning pirates.

sentences.zh: 事方議行，會宗設黨中林、望古多羅逸出之舟，為暴風飄至朝鮮。

translations.literal: The matter was just being deliberated for implementation when among Sōsetsu's party, the boat of Nakabayashi and Mogadorō, blown by storm, drifted to Korea.
translations.idiomatic: While the matter was still under deliberation, a boat carrying Nakabayashi and Mogadorō, who had escaped from Sōsetsu's faction, was blown by storm to Korea.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮人擊斬三十級，生擒二賊以獻。

translations.literal: Koreans struck and beheaded thirty men, capturing two bandits alive and presenting them.
translations.idiomatic: Koreans killed thirty of them and captured two raiders alive, whom they sent as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 給事中夏言因請逮赴浙江，會所司與素卿雜治，因遣給事中劉稍、御史王道往。

translations.literal: Submitter Xia Yan thereupon requested they be sent to Zhejiang, to be jointly tried together with the responsible offices and Suqing; accordingly Submitter Liu Shao and Censor Wang Dao were dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Submitter Xia Yan then asked that the prisoners be sent to Zhejiang for joint trial with the local authorities and Suqing. Submitter Liu Shao and Censor Wang Dao were dispatched for the purpose.

sentences.zh: 至四年，獄成，素卿及中林、望古多羅並論死，系獄。

translations.literal: By the fourth year the case was concluded; Suqing and Nakabayashi and Mogadorō were all sentenced to death and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth year the case was closed. Suqing, Nakabayashi, and Mogadorō were all sentenced to death and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 久之，皆瘐死。

translations.literal: After a long time, they all died of wasting illness.
translations.idiomatic: In time, every one of them wasted away and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 時有琉球使臣鄭繩歸國，命傳諭日本以擒獻宗設，還袁璡及海濱被掠之人，否則閉關絕貢，徐議征討。

translations.literal: At that time the Ryukyuan envoy Zheng Sheng was returning to his country; the court ordered him to convey instructions to Japan to capture and deliver up Sōsetsu, return Yuan Jin and the persons plundered along the coast, or else close the passes and cut off tribute, and discuss punitive action in due course.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ryukyuan envoy Zheng Sheng was about to return home, the court instructed him to tell Japan to hand over Sōsetsu, restore Yuan Jin and the coastal captives, and otherwise face closed borders, an end to tribute, and eventual military punishment.

sentences.zh: 九年，琉球使臣蔡瀚者，道經日本，其王源義晴附表言：「向因本國多事，干戈梗道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the Ryukyuan envoy Cai Han, passing through Japan, had attached to him a memorial from the Japanese ruler Yoshiharu stating: 'Previously, because our country had many troubles, arms blocked the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, the Ryukyuan envoy Cai Han traveled through Japan, where Yoshiharu attached a memorial reading: 'Our realm has been torn by internal strife, and war has obstructed the route.

sentences.zh: 正德勘合不達東都，以故素卿捧弘治勘合行，乞貸遣。

translations.literal: The Zhengde tally slips did not reach the eastern capital; for this reason Suqing carried the Hongzhi tally slips on the journey, and begs that he be allowed to depart.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhengde tallies never reached the eastern capital, so Suqing carried Hongzhi-era tallies instead and asked permission to proceed.

sentences.zh: 望並賜新勘合、金印，修貢如常。」

translations.literal: We hope that new tally slips and a gold seal may also be granted, and tribute restored as before.'
translations.idiomatic: We ask that new tallies and a gold seal be issued so that tribute may resume as usual.'

sentences.zh: 禮官驗其文，無印篆，言：「倭譎詐難信，宜敕琉球王傳諭，仍遵前命。」

translations.literal: The ritual officials examined the document and found no seal impression; they said: 'The Wo are crafty and hard to trust; the king of Ryukyu should be instructed to convey the message, and the previous order should still be followed.'
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Rites inspected the letter and found no seal. They argued that Japanese deceit could not be trusted and that Ryukyu should relay the earlier demand unchanged.'

sentences.zh: 十八年七月，義晴貢使至寧波，守臣以聞。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighteenth year, Yoshiharu's tribute envoys reached Ningbo, and the local officials reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighteenth year, Yoshiharu's tribute mission arrived at Ningbo, and the local authorities notified the court.

sentences.zh: 時不通貢者已十七年，敕巡按御史督同三司官核，果誠心效順，如制遣送，否則卻回，且嚴居民交通之禁。

translations.literal: At that time tribute had been cut off for seventeen years; an imperial order directed the touring censor to supervise the three provincial offices in verifying the mission. If they were truly sincere in submission, they were to be escorted according to regulation; otherwise they were to be turned back, and the prohibition on private contact with residents was to be strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Japan had sent no tribute for seventeen years. The emperor ordered the touring censor, together with the three provincial commissioners, to investigate. If the mission proved genuinely submissive, it would be escorted according to precedent; if not, it would be sent home, and private dealings with local people would be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，貢使碩鼎等至京申前請，乞賜嘉靖新勘合，還素卿及原留貢物。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, the tribute envoys Shuo Ding and others reached the capital and renewed the earlier request, begging for new Jiajing tally slips and the return of Suqing and the tribute goods originally detained.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the second month, the envoys led by Shuo Ding reached Beijing and repeated their request for new Jiajing tallies, Suqing's release, and the return of the detained tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 部議：「勘合不可遽給，務繳舊易新。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated: 'Tally slips must not be granted hastily; the old ones must be surrendered before new ones are exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry advised: 'Tallies should not be issued prematurely; the old slips must be turned in before new ones are given.

sentences.zh: 貢期限十年，人不過百，舟不過三，余不可許。」

translations.literal: The tribute interval is ten years; the number of persons must not exceed one hundred, and ships must not exceed three; nothing beyond this may be permitted.'
translations.idiomatic: Tribute may come only once every ten years, with no more than one hundred men and three ships; no other demands should be granted.'

sentences.zh: 詔如議。

translations.literal: An edict followed the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 二十三年七月復來貢，未及期，且無表文。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year they came again with tribute, before the appointed term and without a formal memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year they presented tribute again, arriving before the scheduled interval and without the required memorial.

sentences.zh: 部臣謂不當納，卻之。

translations.literal: The ministry officials said they ought not to be received, and they were refused.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry held that the mission should not be accepted, and it was turned away.

sentences.zh: 其人利互市，留海濱不去。

translations.literal: Those men, profiting from mutual trade, remained on the coast and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking profit from illicit trade, the envoys lingered on the coast and refused to depart.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史高節請治沿海文武將吏罪，嚴禁奸豪交通，得旨允行。

translations.literal: The touring censor Gao Jie requested that the civil and military officers of the coast be punished and that contact with smugglers be strictly forbidden; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Gao Jie asked that coastal officials be punished and illicit trade with private brokers be ruthlessly suppressed; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 而內地諸奸利其交易，多為之囊橐，終不能盡絕。

translations.literal: Yet inland schemers profited from the trade and often served as their backers and purses, and in the end the traffic could not be wholly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Inland merchants still profited from the trade and often bankrolled the envoys, so the traffic was never fully extinguished.

sentences.zh: 二十六年六月，巡按御史楊九澤言：「浙江寧、紹、台、溫皆濱海，界連福建福、興、漳、泉諸郡，有倭患，雖設衛所城池及巡海副使、備倭都指揮，但海寇出沒無常，兩地官弁不能通攝，制御為難。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-sixth year, the touring censor Yang Jiuzhe said: 'In Zhejiang, Ningbo, Shaoxing, Taizhou, and Wenzhou all border the sea and adjoin Fujian's Fu, Xing, Zhang, and Quan prefectures; there is Wo trouble. Although guard posts, walled cities, coastal vice commissioners, and anti-Wo commanders-in-chief have been established, the sea bandits appear and vanish without fixed pattern, and officers of the two regions cannot exercise joint command, making control difficult.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-sixth year, Touring Censor Yang Jiuzhe reported that Zhejiang's coastal prefectures and the adjoining Fujian ports were all menaced by Japanese raiders. Guard posts and anti-piracy officers existed, but pirates struck unpredictably, and officials in the two provinces could not coordinate, leaving defense ineffective.

sentences.zh: 請如往例，特遣巡視重臣，盡統海濱諸郡，庶事權歸一，威令易行。」

translations.literal: I request that, as in former precedent, a high minister be specially dispatched to tour and oversee all the coastal prefectures, so that authority may be unified and orders easily enforced.'
translations.idiomatic: He asked that a senior envoy be sent, as in earlier practice, to command all coastal prefectures so that authority and enforcement would be unified.'

sentences.zh: 廷議稱善，乃命副都御史硃紈巡撫浙江兼制福、興、漳、泉、建寧五府軍事。

translations.literal: The court deliberation approved this, and Vice Censor-in-chief Zhu Wan was appointed grand coordinator of Zhejiang with concurrent control over the military affairs of Fu, Xing, Zhang, Quan, and Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed, and Vice Censor-in-chief Zhu Wan was made grand coordinator of Zhejiang with military authority over five Fujian prefectures as well.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其王義晴遣使周良等先期來貢，用舟四，人六百，泊於海外，以待明年貢期。

translations.literal: Before long, King Yoshiharu dispatched envoys led by Zhou Liang to come with tribute ahead of schedule, using four ships and six hundred men; they anchored offshore to await the tribute term of the following year.
