translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yoshiharu sent Zhou Liang and others ahead of schedule with four ships and six hundred men, anchoring offshore until the next year's tribute season.

sentences.zh: 守臣沮之，則以風為解。

translations.literal: When local officials tried to stop them, they pleaded adverse winds.
translations.idiomatic: When local officials tried to block them, they claimed they had been delayed by storms.

sentences.zh: 十一月事聞，帝以先期非制，且人船越額，敕守臣勒回。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported in the eleventh month, the emperor, holding that arriving early was against regulation and that the numbers of men and ships exceeded the quota, ordered the local officials to compel them to return.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court in the eleventh month, the emperor ruled that the early arrival and excess men and ships violated precedent and ordered local officials to send the mission home.

sentences.zh: 十二月，倭賊犯寧、台二郡，大肆殺掠，二郡將吏並獲罪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Wo bandits raided the two prefectures of Ning and Tai, slaughtering and plundering on a great scale; the officers of both prefectures were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Japanese raiders struck Ningbo and Taizhou, killing and looting widely, and the officials of both prefectures were punished.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，周良復求貢，紈以聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year, Zhou Liang again requested to present tribute, and Wan reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the sixth month, Zhou Liang again asked to present tribute, and Zhu Wan reported it to the court.

sentences.zh: 禮部言：「日本貢期及舟與人數雖違制，第表辭恭順，去貢期亦不遠，若概加拒絕，則航海之勞可憫，若稍務含容，則宗設、素卿之事可鑑。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said: 'Although Japan's tribute term and the numbers of ships and men violate regulation, the memorial language is respectful and submissive, and the proper tribute season is not far off. If they are wholly rejected, the hardship of the sea voyage deserves pity; yet if too much indulgence is shown, the cases of Sōsetsu and Suqing may serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites argued that although the mission broke the rules on timing, ships, and personnel, its language was deferential and the proper tribute season was near. Outright rejection would ignore the hardship of the voyage, yet excessive leniency would repeat the mistakes made with Sōsetsu and Suqing.

sentences.zh: 宜敕紈循十八年例，起送五十人，余留嘉賓館，量加犒賞，諭令歸國。

translations.literal: Wan should be instructed to follow the precedent of the eighteenth year: escort fifty men to the capital, leave the rest at the Guest Lodge, grant rewards in measured amount, and instruct them to return to their country.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wan should follow the eighteenth-year precedent: send fifty envoys onward to the capital, house the rest at the Guest Lodge, reward them moderately, and order them home.

sentences.zh: 若互市防守事，宜在紈善處之。」

translations.literal: As for matters of mutual trade and coastal defense, Wan should handle them well.'
translations.idiomatic: Trade restrictions and coastal defense should be left to Zhu Wan's judgment.'

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 紈力言五十人過少，乃令百人赴都。

translations.literal: Wan strongly argued that fifty men were too few, and so one hundred men were ordered to proceed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wan protested that fifty men were too few, and the court allowed one hundred to go to the capital.

sentences.zh: 部議 但賞百人，余罷勿賞。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated: only the one hundred men were to be rewarded; the rest were dismissed and not rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ruled that only the hundred envoys sent to court would receive rewards; the others would get nothing.

sentences.zh: 良訴貢舟高大。

translations.literal: Liang complained that the tribute ships were large and tall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Liang protested that the tribute vessels were unusually large.

sentences.zh: 勢須五百人。

translations.literal: They necessarily required five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Such ships, he said, required five hundred men to crew.

sentences.zh: 中國商舶入海，往往藏匿島中為寇，故增一舟防寇，非敢違制。

translations.literal: Chinese merchant ships entering the sea often hid on islands and turned to piracy; therefore one extra ship had been added to guard against bandits, not from any intent to violate regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese merchant vessels often sheltered on islands and became pirates, he explained, so an extra ship had been added for protection, not to defy the rules.

sentences.zh: 部議量增其賞，且謂：「百人之制，彼國勢難遵行，宜相其貢舟大小，以施禁令。」

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated to increase their rewards accordingly, and further said: 'The hundred-man rule is hard for their country to observe; the prohibition should be applied according to the size of the tribute ships.'
translations.idiomatic: The ministry agreed to increase the rewards and added that the hundred-man limit was impractical for Japan; restrictions should be scaled to the size of the tribute fleet.'

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 日本故有孝、武兩朝勘合幾二百道，使臣前此入貢請易新者，而令繳其舊。

translations.literal: Japan originally possessed nearly two hundred tally slips from the Xiaojing and Wu eras; when envoys had previously come to request new ones, they were ordered to surrender the old.
translations.idiomatic: Japan once held nearly two hundred tally slips from the Xiaojing and Wu reigns, and earlier missions had been required to surrender old slips before receiving new ones.

sentences.zh: 至是良持弘治勘合十五道，言其餘為素卿子所竊，捕之不獲。

translations.literal: On this occasion Liang held fifteen Hongzhi tally slips and said the rest had been stolen by Suqing's son, whom they had been unable to capture.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhou Liang produced fifteen Hongzhi tallies and claimed the rest had been stolen by Suqing's son, who could not be caught.

sentences.zh: 正德勘合留十五道為信，而以四十道來還。

translations.literal: Fifteen Zhengde tally slips were retained as proof, while forty slips were brought back and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen Zhengde tallies were kept as evidence, and forty were returned.

sentences.zh: 部議令異時悉繳舊，乃許易新，亦報可。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that when the old slips were all surrendered at a later time, new ones would then be granted; this too was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ruled that new tallies would be issued only after all old ones were surrendered; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 當是時，日本王雖入貢，其各島諸倭歲常侵掠，濱海奸民又往往勾之。

translations.literal: At that time, although the king of Japan sent tribute, the various islands' Wo raided every year, and coastal traitors often colluded with them.
translations.idiomatic: Even while the Japanese king sent tribute, raiders from the outlying islands attacked yearly, often aided by coastal collaborators.

sentences.zh: 紈乃嚴為申禁，獲交通者，不俟命輒以便宜斬之。

translations.literal: Wan therefore enforced prohibitions strictly; when he captured persons engaged in illicit contact, he executed them on his own authority without awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wan enforced the bans ruthlessly, summarily executing anyone caught trading with the Japanese without waiting for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 由是，浙、閩大姓素為倭內主者，失利而怨。

translations.literal: Thereupon the great clans of Zhe and Min who had long served as the Wo's agents inland lost profit and nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful Zhejiang and Fujian clans that had long brokered trade with the Japanese lost their profits and turned against him.

sentences.zh: 紈又數騰疏於朝，顯言大姓通倭狀，以故閩、浙人皆惡之，而閩尤甚。

translations.literal: Wan also repeatedly sent memorials to the court openly describing how the great clans communicated with the Wo; for this reason the people of Min and Zhe all hated him, and those of Min especially so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wan also sent repeated memorials exposing great-clan collusion with Japan, earning hatred throughout Fujian and Zhejiang, above all in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史周亮，閩產也，上疏詆紈，請改巡撫為巡視，以殺其權。

translations.literal: The touring censor Zhou Liang, a native of Min, submitted a memorial slandering Wan and asking that the grand coordinator be reduced to a touring inspector, so as to diminish his power.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Zhou Liang, a Fujian native, attacked Zhu Wan in a memorial and asked that his title be reduced from grand coordinator to touring inspector, stripping him of real authority.

sentences.zh: 其黨在朝者左右之，竟如其請。

translations.literal: His faction in court supported him from both sides, and in the end his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His allies at court maneuvered on his behalf, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 又奪紈官。

translations.literal: Wan's office was also taken from him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wan was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 羅織其擅殺罪，紈自殺。

translations.literal: They fabricated charges of unauthorized killing against him, and Wan killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was framed for unauthorized executions and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 自是不置巡撫者四年，海禁復弛，亂益滋甚。

translations.literal: From this time no grand coordinator was appointed for four years; the maritime ban slackened again, and disorder grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: For four years thereafter no grand coordinator was appointed, the sea ban collapsed, and the crisis worsened.

sentences.zh: 祖制，浙江設市舶提舉司，以中官主之，駐寧波。

translations.literal: By ancestral institution, Zhejiang had a Maritime Trade Supervisorate, headed by a eunuch stationed at Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: Under the founding institutions, Zhejiang maintained a Maritime Trade Supervisorate at Ningbo under a eunuch director.

sentences.zh: 海舶至則平其直，制馭之權在上。

translations.literal: When overseas ships arrived, prices were fixed and the power of control lay with the court.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign ships arrived, the state set prices and kept trade under central control.

sentences.zh: 及世宗，盡撤天下鎮守中官，並撤市舶，而濱海奸人遂操其利。

translations.literal: Under the Shizong emperor, all the empire's garrison eunuchs were withdrawn, and the trade offices were abolished as well; then coastal schemers seized the profits for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong, garrison eunuchs and trade offices were abolished nationwide, and coastal smugglers took over the profits.

sentences.zh: 初市猶商主之，及嚴通番之禁，遂移之貴官家，負其直者愈甚。

translations.literal: At first the market was still run by merchants; when the ban on overseas trade was tightened, it shifted into the houses of great officials, and those owed payment suffered all the more.
translations.idiomatic: At first merchants still controlled the trade, but as the ban on overseas commerce tightened, business moved into the mansions of powerful officials, and unpaid debts mounted.

sentences.zh: 索之急，則以危言嚇之，或又以好言紿之，謂我終不負若直。

translations.literal: When collection was pressed urgently, they would threaten with alarming words, or else deceive with fair promises, saying they would never fail to pay what was owed.
translations.idiomatic: When creditors pressed for payment, the powerful either threatened them or soothed them with empty promises that the debt would someday be honored.

sentences.zh: 倭喪其貲不得返，已大恨，而大奸若汪直、徐海、陳東、麻葉輩素窟其中，以內地不得逞，悉逸海島為主謀。

translations.literal: The Wo, having lost their goods and unable to return, already hated this deeply; and great villains such as Wang Zhi, Xu Hai, Chen Dong, and Ma Ye had long lurked among them. Unable to operate inland, they all fled to the islands and became chief plotters.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese, cheated of their goods and unable to go home, were already furious; and ringleaders such as Wang Zhi, Xu Hai, Chen Dong, and Ma Ye, driven from the mainland, made their bases on the islands.

sentences.zh: 倭聽指揮，誘之入寇。

translations.literal: The Wo obeyed their commands and were enticed to raid inland.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese followed their lead and were lured into raids on the mainland.

sentences.zh: 海中巨盜，遂襲倭服飾、旂號，並分艘掠內地，無不大利，故倭患日劇，於是廷議復設巡撫。

translations.literal: Great sea bandits thereupon donned Wo dress and banners, divided their fleets, and plundered inland, always with great profit; thus the Wo trouble grew daily worse, and the court deliberated restoring the grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Major pirates then adopted Japanese dress and banners, split into fleets, and raided inland with enormous profit, so the crisis intensified until the court decided to restore the grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 三十一年七月以僉都御史王忬任之，而勢已不可撲滅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirty-first year, Vice Censor-in-chief Wang Yu was appointed to the post, but the situation was already beyond suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the thirty-first year, Vice Censor-in-chief Wang Yu was appointed grand coordinator, but the disaster was already uncontrollable.

sentences.zh: 明初，沿海要地建衛所，設戰船，董以都司、巡視、副使等官，控制周密。

translations.literal: In the early Ming, guard posts were built at key points along the coast, war ships were deployed, and regional commanders, touring inspectors, and vice commissioners were appointed to oversee them; control was thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, coastal guard posts and warships were established under regional commanders and anti-piracy officers, and the system was tightly organized.

sentences.zh: 迨承平久，船敝伍虛。

translations.literal: After long peace, the ships decayed and the ranks stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Years of peace left the fleet rotting and the garrisons hollow.

sentences.zh: 及遇警，乃募漁船以資哨守。

translations.literal: When alarms came, fishing boats had to be hired for patrol and defense.
translations.idiomatic: When danger arose, patrol duty fell to hired fishing boats.

sentences.zh: 兵非素練，船非專業，見寇舶至，輒望風逃匿，而上又無統率御之。

translations.literal: The troops were not trained by routine, the ships were not professional craft; when enemy vessels appeared, they would flee at sight of the wind, and above them there was no commander to lead resistance.
translations.idiomatic: The men were untrained, the boats makeshift; at the first sight of enemy sails they fled, and no commander above them could impose order.

sentences.zh: 以故賊帆所指，無不殘破。

translations.literal: For this reason, wherever the bandits' sails pointed, nothing escaped ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the raiders turned, devastation followed.

sentences.zh: 三十二年三月，汪直勾諸倭大舉入寇，連艦數百，蔽海而至。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-second year, Wang Zhi incited the various Wo to raid on a great scale; several hundred linked ships covered the sea as they arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirty-second year, Wang Zhi rallied the Japanese for a massive raid; hundreds of linked ships blackened the sea.

sentences.zh: 浙東、西，江南、北，濱海數千里，同時告警。

translations.literal: Eastern and western Zhejiang, southern and northern Jiangnan, and thousands of li of coast raised alarms at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Alarms sounded at once along thousands of li of coast from eastern and western Zhejiang to north and south Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 破昌國衛。

translations.literal: They broke Changguo Guard.
translations.idiomatic: They overran Changguo Guard.

sentences.zh: 四月犯太倉，破上海縣，掠江陰，攻乍浦。

translations.literal: In the fourth month they raided Taicang, broke Shanghai County, plundered Jiangyin, and attacked Zhapu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they struck Taicang, sacked Shanghai County, looted Jiangyin, and assaulted Zhapu.

sentences.zh: 八月劫金山衛，犯崇明及常熟、嘉定。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they robbed Jinshan Guard and raided Chongming, Changshu, and Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they pillaged Jinshan Guard and hit Chongming, Changshu, and Jiading.

sentences.zh: 三十三年正月自太倉掠蘇州，攻松江，復趨江北，薄通、泰。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirty-third year they plundered Suzhou from Taicang, attacked Songjiang, then turned toward the north bank and pressed on Tong and Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirty-third year they swept from Taicang into Suzhou, struck Songjiang, then crossed to the north bank and threatened Tongzhou and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 四月陷嘉善，破崇明，復薄蘇州，入崇德縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month they took Jiashan, broke Chongming, again pressed on Suzhou, and entered Chongde County.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they captured Jiashan, broke Chongming, threatened Suzhou again, and entered Chongde County.

sentences.zh: 六月由吳江掠嘉興，還屯柘林。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they plundered Jiaxing from Wujiang and returned to encamp at Zhelin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they raided Jiaxing from Wujiang and withdrew to camp at Zhelin.

sentences.zh: 縱橫來往，若入無人之境，忬亦不能有所為。

translations.literal: They moved to and fro as if entering an uninhabited land, and Yu too could accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: They ranged freely as though the country were empty, and Wang Yu could do nothing to stop them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，忬改撫大同，以李天寵代，又命兵部尚書張經總督軍務。

translations.literal: Before long, Yu was transferred to grand coordination of Datong, Li Tianchong replaced him, and Minister of War Zhang Jing was appointed supreme commander of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Yu was moved to Datong, Li Tianchong replaced him, and War Minister Zhang Jing was made supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 乃大徵兵四方，協力進剿。

translations.literal: Thereupon troops were levied on a large scale from all quarters to advance jointly in extermination.
translations.idiomatic: The court then mobilized troops from across the empire for a coordinated campaign.

sentences.zh: 是時，倭以川沙窪、柘林為巢，抄掠四出。

translations.literal: At that time the Wo made their nests at Chuanshawa and Zhelin and sent raiding parties in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders made bases at Chuanshawa and Zhelin and launched raids in every direction.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，賊奪舟犯乍浦、海寧，陷崇德，轉掠塘棲、新市、橫塘、雙林等處，攻德清縣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, the bandits seized boats and raided Zhapu and Haining, took Chongde, turned to plunder Tangqi, Xinshi, Hengtang, Shuanglin, and other places, and attacked Deqing County.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the first month, they seized boats, hit Zhapu and Haining, captured Chongde, swept through Tangqi, Xinshi, Hengtang, Shuanglin, and other towns, and assaulted Deqing County.

sentences.zh: 五月復合新倭，突犯嘉興，至王江涇，乃為經擊斬千九百餘級，余奔柘林。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they joined with fresh Wo raiders, suddenly struck Jiaxing, and reached Wangjiangjing; there Jing cut down more than nineteen hundred of them, and the rest fled to Zhelin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they united with newly arrived raiders, burst into Jiaxing, and reached Wangjiangjing, where Zhang Jing killed more than nineteen hundred of them and drove the rest back to Zhelin.

sentences.zh: 其他倭復掠蘇州境，延及江陰、無錫，出入太湖。

translations.literal: Other Wo bands plundered the Suzhou region, extending the damage to Jiangyin and Wuxi and passing in and out of Lake Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Other raiding bands looted Suzhou prefecture, spread into Jiangyin and Wuxi, and ranged across Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 大抵真倭十之三，從倭者十之七。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, true Wo were three parts in ten; followers among the Wo were seven parts in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly speaking, only three tenths were genuine Japanese; seven tenths were Chinese collaborators dressed as Wo.

sentences.zh: 倭戰則驅其所掠之人為軍鋒，法嚴，人皆致死，而官軍素懦怯，所至潰奔。

translations.literal: When the Wo fought, they drove the persons they had captured to serve as battle van; discipline was strict, and all fought to the death, while the government troops were by nature cowardly and fled in rout wherever they went.
translations.idiomatic: In battle the raiders drove captives ahead as human shields under harsh discipline, while government troops, habitually timid, broke and ran at every encounter.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣工部侍郎趙文華督察軍情。

translations.literal: The emperor then dispatched Vice Minister of Works Zhao Wenhua to inspect military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Vice Minister of Works Zhao Wenhua to supervise the campaign.

sentences.zh: 文華顛倒功罪，諸軍益解體。

translations.literal: Wenhua inverted merit and guilt, and the armies disintegrated all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenhua reversed reward and punishment, and the armies fell apart.

sentences.zh: 經、天寵並被逮，代以周珫、胡宗憲。

translations.literal: Zhang Jing and Li Tianchong were both arrested; Zhou Yan and Hu Zongxian replaced them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing and Li Tianchong were arrested and replaced by Zhou Yan and Hu Zongxian.

sentences.zh: 逾月，珫罷，代以楊宜。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Yan was dismissed and Yang Yi replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month Zhou Yan was removed and Yang Yi took his place.

sentences.zh: 時賊勢蔓延，江浙無不蹂躪。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits' power spread, and there was no part of Jiangsu and Zhejiang that was not trampled.
translations.idiomatic: By then the raiders had spread across Jiangsu and Zhejiang, leaving scarcely a district untouched.

sentences.zh: 新倭來益眾，益肆毒。

translations.literal: Newly arriving Wo grew ever more numerous and ever more vicious.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh Japanese raiders kept arriving in greater numbers and with greater ferocity.

sentences.zh: 每自焚其舟，登岸劫掠。

translations.literal: They often burned their own ships, came ashore, and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: They routinely burned their ships after landing and then looted inland.

sentences.zh: 自杭州北新關西剽淳安，突徽州歙縣，至績溪、旌德，過涇縣，趨南陵，遂達蕪湖。

translations.literal: From Beixin Pass west of Hangzhou they plundered Chun'an, suddenly struck She County in Huizhou, reached Jixi and Jingde, passed Jing County, pressed on to Nanling, and so reached Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Starting west of Hangzhou at Beixin Pass, they looted Chun'an, burst into She County in Huizhou, pushed through Jixi and Jingde, crossed Jing County, reached Nanling, and advanced as far as Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 燒南岸，奔太平府，犯江寧鎮，徑侵南京。

translations.literal: They burned the south bank, fled toward Taiping Prefecture, raided Jiangning Guard, and directly invaded Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: They burned the south bank of the Yangtze, raced toward Taiping Prefecture, struck Jiangning Guard, and pressed on to Nanjing itself.

sentences.zh: 倭紅衣黃蓋，率眾犯大安德門，及夾岡，乃趨秣陵關而去，由溧水流劫溧陽、宜興。

translations.literal: The Wo, in red coats and yellow canopies, led their masses to raid the Great Virtue Gate and Jiogang, then turned toward Muling Pass and departed, flowing down the Lishui to plunder Liyang and Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Clad in red and bearing yellow banners, the raiders hit Nanjing's Great Virtue Gate and Jiogang, then withdrew through Muling Pass and descended the Lishui River to loot Liyang and Yixing.

sentences.zh: 聞官兵自太湖出，遂越武進，抵無錫，駐惠山。

translations.literal: When they heard that government troops were coming out from Lake Tai, they crossed into Wujin, reached Wuxi, and encamped at Huishan.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that troops were moving out from Lake Tai, they crossed into Wujin, reached Wuxi, and camped on Huishan.

sentences.zh: 一晝夜奔百八十餘里，抵滸墅。

translations.literal: In one day and one night they ran more than one hundred and eighty li and reached Xushu.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day and night they marched more than one hundred and eighty li to Xushu.

sentences.zh: 為官軍所圍，追及於楊林橋，殲之。

translations.literal: They were surrounded by government troops, pursued to Yanglin Bridge, and annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops surrounded them, caught them at Yanglin Bridge, and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 是役也，賊不過六七十人，而經行數千里，殺戮戰傷者幾四千人，歷八十餘日始滅，此三十四年九月事也。

translations.literal: In this campaign the bandits numbered no more than sixty or seventy men, yet they traveled several thousand li, killed and wounded nearly four thousand persons, and were not destroyed until more than eighty days had passed; this was in the ninth month of the thirty-fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: In that operation fewer than seventy raiders marched thousands of li, killed or wounded nearly four thousand people, and survived more than eighty days before they were finally destroyed in the ninth month of the thirty-fourth year.

sentences.zh: 應天巡撫曹邦輔以捷聞，文華忌其功。

translations.literal: Cao Bangfu, grand coordinator of Yingtian, reported the victory, and Wenhua resented his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Cao Bangfu reported the victory, and Zhao Wenhua resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 以倭之巢於陶宅也，乃大集浙、直兵，與宗憲親將之。

translations.literal: Because the Wo had their nest at Taozhai, he gathered troops from Zhe and Zhili on a large scale and personally led them with Zongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Claiming the raiders were based at Taozhai, Zhao Wenhua massed troops from Zhejiang and the capital region and took the field in person with Hu Zongxian.

sentences.zh: 又約邦輔合剿，分道並進，營於松江之甎橋。

translations.literal: He also arranged with Bangfu for a joint extermination, advancing by separate routes and encamping at Zhuan Bridge in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He also arranged a joint strike with Cao Bangfu, dividing forces and encamping at Zhuan Bridge in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 倭悉銳來沖，遂大敗，文華氣奪，賊益熾。

translations.literal: The Wo brought all their crack troops to charge; they were utterly defeated, Wenhua's spirit was broken, and the bandits grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders threw their best troops into the assault, routed Wenhua's force, broke his morale, and grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 十月，倭自樂清登岸，流劫黃岩、仙居、奉化、餘姚、上虞，被殺擄者無算。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Wo bandits landed from Yueqing and flowed in raiding through Huangyan, Xianju, Fenghua, Yuyao, and Shangyu; those killed and captured were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month raiders landed at Yueqing and swept through Huangyan, Xianju, Fenghua, Yuyao, and Shangyu, killing and capturing beyond number.

sentences.zh: 至嵊縣乃殲之，亦不滿二百人，顧深入三府，歷五十日始平。

translations.literal: At Sheng County they were finally annihilated; they numbered no more than two hundred men, yet they had penetrated three prefectures and were not pacified until fifty days had passed.
translations.idiomatic: They were finally destroyed at Sheng County. Though fewer than two hundred strong, they had plunged deep into three prefectures and took fifty days to suppress.

sentences.zh: 其先一枝自山東日照流劫東安衛，至淮安、贛榆、沭陽、桃源，至清河阻雨，為徐、邳官兵所殲，亦不過數十人，流害千里，殺戮千餘，其悍如此。

translations.literal: Earlier, one band from Rizhao in Shandong flowed in raiding through Dong'an Guard, reaching Huaian, Ganyu, Shuyang, and Taoyuan; at Qinghe they were blocked by rain and annihilated by the government troops of Xu and Pi. They numbered no more than several tens of men, yet their flowing harm extended a thousand li and their slaughter exceeded a thousand — such was their ferocity.
translations.idiomatic: One band had set out from Rizhao in Shandong, raiding through Dong'an Guard and on through Huaian, Ganyu, Shuyang, and Taoyuan before rain trapped them at Qinghe, where Xu- and Pi-area government troops wiped them out. Fewer than fifty men had ravaged a thousand li and killed more than a thousand people — that was how fierce they were.

sentences.zh: 而文華自甎橋之敗，見倭寇勢甚，其自柘林移於周浦，與泊於川沙舊巢及嘉定高橋者自如，他侵犯者無虛日，文華乃以寇息請還朝。

translations.literal: As for Wenhua, after the defeat at Zhuan Bridge he saw that the Wo bandits' power was very great. They moved from Zhelin to Zhoupu, while those anchored at the old nests of Chuansha and Jiading Gaoqiao carried on as before, and other incursions occurred without a single idle day. Wenhua then requested to return to court on the grounds that the bandits had been quelled.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat at Zhuan Bridge, Zhao Wenhua saw how strong the pirates had become. They shifted from Zhelin to Zhoupu, their comrades at the old bases in Chuansha and Jiading Gaoqiao carried on as before, and fresh raids came almost daily. Zhao Wenhua then asked to go back to court, claiming the threat was over.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，罷宜，代以宗憲，以阮鶚巡撫浙江。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, Yi was dismissed and replaced by Zongxian, and Ruan E was made grand coordinator of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the second month, Yang Yi was removed and Hu Zongxian took his place; Ruan E was appointed grand coordinator of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 於是宗憲乃請遣使諭日本國王，禁戢島寇，招還通番奸商，許立功免罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zongxian requested to send envoys to instruct the king of Japan to restrain the island bandits, recall the illicit merchants who traded with the foreigners, and promise that merit would win exemption from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zongxian then proposed sending envoys to warn the Japanese king to rein in the island raiders, summon back Chinese smugglers who had gone over to them, and offer pardons in exchange for loyal service.

sentences.zh: 既得旨，遂遣寧波諸生蔣洲、陳可願往。

translations.literal: Once he had received the imperial rescript, he sent the Ningbo scholars Jiang Zhou and Chen Keyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After imperial approval, he dispatched the Ningbo scholars Jiang Zhou and Chen Keyuan.

sentences.zh: 及是，可願還，言至其國五島，遇汪直、毛海峰，謂日本內亂，王與其相俱死，諸島不相統攝，須遍諭乃可杜其入犯。

translations.literal: At this time Keyuan returned and reported that he had reached the Gotō Islands of that country, where he met Wang Zhi and Mao Haifeng. They said that Japan was torn by internal disorder, that the king and his chancellor had both died, and that the islands were not under unified control; only by issuing proclamations everywhere could their invasions be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chen Keyuan had returned. He reported reaching Japan's Gotō Islands, where he met Wang Zhi and Mao Haifeng. They claimed Japan was in civil turmoil, that both the king and his chief minister were dead, and that the islands answered to no single authority — only a broad round of proclamations could stop the raids.

sentences.zh: 又言，有薩摩洲者，雖已揚帆入寇，非其本心，乞通貢互市，願殺賊自效。

translations.literal: He also reported that in Satsuma, though its people had already set sail to raid, this was not their true intent; they begged to open tribute and mutual trade and were willing to kill bandits to prove their loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He added that Satsuma, though already sending raiders, did not truly wish to make war; it sought restored tribute and trade and offered to kill pirates to prove its good faith.

sentences.zh: 乃留洲傳諭各島，而送可願還。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhou was then kept behind to convey instructions to the various islands, and Keyuan was sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhou remained to carry the message to the islands while Chen Keyuan was sent home.

sentences.zh: 宗憲以聞，兵部言：「直等本編民，既稱效順，即當釋兵。

translations.literal: Zongxian reported this, and the Ministry of War said: "Zhi and the others were originally registered civilians of the realm. Having declared their submission, they ought at once to lay down arms.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zongxian reported the matter, and the Ministry of War replied: "Wang Zhi and his followers were subjects of the Ming. Now that they claim to submit, they should disarm at once.

sentences.zh: 乃絕不言及，第求開市通貢，隱若屬國然，其奸叵測。

translations.literal: Yet they say nothing of this at all and only seek to open markets and tribute trade, secretly comporting themselves like a subordinate state — their treachery is beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they say nothing about disarming and only press for open markets and tribute trade, acting almost like a vassal state. Their designs are impossible to fathom.

sentences.zh: 宜令督臣振揚國威，嚴加備御。

translations.literal: The supervising officials should be ordered to display the majesty of the state and strengthen defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier commanders should be told to assert imperial authority and tighten coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 移檄直等，俾剿除舟山諸賊巢以自明。

translations.literal: A proclamation should be sent to Zhi and the others requiring them to exterminate the bandit nests in Zhoushan and thereby prove their sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi and his men should be ordered by proclamation to wipe out the pirate nests around Zhoushan and prove their loyalty that way.

sentences.zh: 果海疆廓清，自有恩賚。」

translations.literal: If the sea frontier is truly cleared, rewards will naturally follow."
translations.idiomatic: If they truly pacify the coast, imperial favor will follow.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 時兩浙皆被倭，而慈溪焚殺獨慘，餘姚次之。

translations.literal: At that time both Zhe regions were afflicted by Wo bandits, but the burning and slaughter in Cixi was uniquely severe, and Yuyao ranked next.
translations.idiomatic: Both halves of Zhejiang were under attack, but Cixi suffered the worst burning and slaughter, with Yuyao close behind.

sentences.zh: 浙西柘林、乍浦、烏鎮、皁林間，皆為賊巢，前後至者二萬餘人，命宗憲亟圖方略。

translations.literal: Between Zhelin, Zhapu, Wuzhen, and Zaolin in western Zhejiang, all became bandit nests; those who arrived before and after numbered more than twenty thousand men. Zongxian was ordered to devise a strategy at once.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhejiang from Zhelin and Zhapu to Wuzhen and Zaolin had become a chain of pirate bases holding more than twenty thousand men. Hu Zongxian was ordered to act quickly.

sentences.zh: 七月，宗憲言：「賊首毛海峰自陳可願還，一敗倭寇於舟山，再敗之瀝表，又遣其黨招諭各島，相率效順，乞加重賞。」

translations.literal: In the seventh month Zongxian reported: "The bandit chief Mao Haifeng, since Chen Keyuan's return, has once defeated Wo bandits at Zhoushan and twice at Biaoli, and has also sent his followers to persuade the various islands to submit one after another. He begs for a heavy reward."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Hu Zongxian reported: "Since Chen Keyuan returned, the pirate leader Mao Haifeng has beaten Wo raiders once at Zhoushan and twice at Biaoli, and sent envoys to bring the islands over one by one. He asks for a substantial reward.

sentences.zh: 部令宗憲以便宜行。

translations.literal: The ministry ordered Zongxian to act as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry told Hu Zongxian to use his discretion.

sentences.zh: 當是時，徐海、陳東、麻葉，方連兵攻圍桐鄉，宗憲設計間之，海遂擒東、葉以降，盡殲其餘眾於乍浦。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Hai, Chen Dong, and Ma Ye were jointly attacking and besieging Tongxiang. Zongxian devised a stratagem to set them against one another; Hai then captured Dong and Ye and surrendered, and the rest of their followers were annihilated at Zhapu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hai, Chen Dong, and Ma Ye were then besieging Tongxiang together. Hu Zongxian turned them against one another; Xu Hai seized Chen Dong and Ma Ye and submitted, and their remaining men were destroyed at Zhapu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復蹴海於梁莊，海亦授首，餘黨盡滅。

translations.literal: Before long he again crushed Hai at Liangzhuang; Hai too surrendered his head, and the remaining followers were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hu Zongxian routed Xu Hai at Liangzhuang as well. Hai lost his head, and his last followers were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 江南、浙西諸寇略平，而江北倭則犯丹陽及掠瓜洲，燒漕艘者明春復犯如皋、海門，攻通州，掠揚州、高耶，入寶應，遂侵淮安府，集於廟灣，踰年乃克。

translations.literal: The bandits in Jiangnan and western Zhejiang were largely pacified, but the northern Wo bandits invaded Danyang and plundered Guazhou, burning grain-transport vessels. The next spring they again raided Rugao and Haimen, attacked Tongzhou, plundered Yangzhou and Gaoyou, entered Baoying, and then invaded Huaian Prefecture and gathered at Miaowan; only after a year were they overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Pirates in Jiangnan and western Zhejiang were largely subdued, but northern raiders struck Danyang, looted Guazhou, and burned grain barges. The next spring they hit Rugao and Haimen, attacked Tongzhou, raided Yangzhou and Gaoyou, pushed into Baoying, and finally massed at Miaowan in Huaian Prefecture. A full year passed before they were defeated.

sentences.zh: 其浙東之倭則盤踞於舟山，亦先後為官軍所襲。

translations.literal: The Wo bandits in eastern Zhejiang entrenched themselves at Zhoushan and were also repeatedly attacked by government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Zhejiang's pirates held Zhoushan and were hit again and again by government forces.

sentences.zh: 先是，蔣洲宣諭諸島，至豐後被留，令僧人往山口等島傳諭禁戢。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jiang Zhou was proclaiming instructions to the various islands, he was detained at Bungo and ordered a monk to go to Yamaguchi and other islands to convey the prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Zhou was carrying the imperial message to the islands, he was held at Bungo and had to send a monk onward to Yamaguchi and the other islands with orders to stand down.

sentences.zh: 於是山口都督源義長具咨送還被掠人口，而咨乃用國王印。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minamoto Yoshinaga, the daimyo of Yamaguchi, prepared a memorial and sent back the captured population, and the memorial bore the king's seal.
translations.idiomatic: Minamoto Yoshinaga, lord of Yamaguchi, then sent a memorial returning captives — and the document bore the royal seal.

sentences.zh: 豐後太守源義鎮遣僧德陽等具方物，奉表謝罪，請頒勘合修貢，送洲還。

translations.literal: Minamoto Yoshishige, governor of Bungo, sent the monk Tokuyō and others with local products, submitted a memorial begging pardon, requested the issuance of tally-slips and the restoration of tribute, and sent Zhou back.
translations.idiomatic: Bungo's governor Minamoto Yoshishige sent the monk Tokuyō with gifts, a memorial begging forgiveness, a request for restored tally-slips and tribute relations, and Jiang Zhou's release.

sentences.zh: 前楊宜所遣鄭舜功出海哨探者，行至豐後島，島主亦遣僧清授附舟來謝罪，言前後侵犯，皆中國奸商潛引諸島夷眾，義鎮等實不知。

translations.literal: The patrol sent out to sea earlier by Yang Yi, Zheng Shungong, had reached Bungo Island; the island lord also sent the monk Seiju aboard the returning vessel to beg pardon, saying that the raids before and after had all been secretly led by illicit Chinese merchants who drew in the island barbarians, and that Yoshishige and the others truly had not known.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shungong, whom Yang Yi had sent to scout the seas, had reached Bungo; its lord sent the monk Seiju back on the same boat to apologize, claiming the raids had all been instigated by Chinese smugglers who dragged islanders along and that Yoshishige and his men had known nothing.

sentences.zh: 於是宗憲疏陳其事，言：「洲奉使二年，止歷豐後、山口二島，或有貢物而無印信勘合，或有印信而無國王名稱，皆違朝典。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zongxian memorialized the matter, saying: "Zhou served on his mission for two years and visited only the two islands of Bungo and Yamaguchi. Some brought tribute goods but no sealed tally-slips; some bore seals but no royal name — all of this violates court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zongxian reported the affair, noting that Jiang Zhou had spent two years abroad and reached only Bungo and Yamaguchi. Some missions brought gifts without proper tally-slips; others bore seals without the king's name. All of this fell short of Ming protocol.

sentences.zh: 然彼既以貢來，又送還被掠人口，實有畏罪乞恩意。

translations.literal: Yet since they have come with tribute and have also sent back the captured population, they truly show an intent to fear guilt and beg grace.
translations.idiomatic: Still, they had come bearing tribute and returned captives, which showed genuine fear and a wish for mercy.

sentences.zh: 宜禮遣其使，令傳諭義鎮、義長，轉諭日本王，擒獻倡亂諸渠，及中國奸宄，方許通貢。」

translations.literal: Their envoys should be courteously sent off and instructed to relay to Yoshishige and Yoshinaga, and through them to the king of Japan, that the ringleaders of the disorder and the Chinese traitors must be captured and handed over before tribute trade may be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Their envoys should be sent home with courtesy and told to inform Yoshishige and Yoshinaga, and through them the Japanese king, that trade would resume only after the ringleaders and Chinese collaborators were captured and delivered.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 汪直之踞海島也，與其黨王滶、葉宗滿、謝和、王清溪等，各挾倭寇為雄。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhi held the sea islands, he and his followers Wang Ao, Ye Zongman, Xie He, and Wang Qingxi each relied on Wo bandits to make themselves powerful.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Zhi held the offshore islands, he and his lieutenants Wang Ao, Ye Zongman, Xie He, and Wang Qingxi each built power by allying with Japanese raiders.

sentences.zh: 朝廷至懸伯爵、萬金之賞以購之，迄不能致。

translations.literal: The court even offered the reward of a marquisate and ten thousand taels of gold to capture him, yet to the end could not obtain him.
translations.idiomatic: The court put a marquisate and ten thousand taels of gold on his head, yet never managed to take him.

sentences.zh: 及是，內地官軍頗有備，倭雖橫，亦多被剿戮，有全島無一人歸者，往往怨直，直漸不自安。

translations.literal: By this time the inland government troops were fairly well prepared; though the Wo bandits were rampant, many were also exterminated, and some whole islands saw not a single man return. They often blamed Zhi, and Zhi gradually lost his sense of security.
translations.idiomatic: Inland defenses had improved by then. Raiders still roamed widely, but many were cut down, and some islands lost every man who sailed out. Resentment turned on Wang Zhi, and he grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 宗憲與直同郡，館直母與其妻孥於杭州，遣蔣洲齎其家書招之。

translations.literal: Zongxian was from the same prefecture as Zhi. He lodged Zhi's mother and his wife and children at Hangzhou and sent Jiang Zhou carrying a letter from the family to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zongxian came from the same home region as Wang Zhi. He housed Wang's mother, wife, and children in Hangzhou and sent Jiang Zhou with a letter from the family to summon him in.

sentences.zh: 直知家屬固無恙，頗心動。

translations.literal: When Zhi learned that his family was indeed unharmed, he was somewhat moved in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that his family was safe, Wang Zhi wavered.

sentences.zh: 義鎮等以中國許互市，亦喜。

translations.literal: Yoshishige and the others, because China had promised mutual trade, were also pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yoshishige and his allies were pleased as well, since China had promised trade.

sentences.zh: 乃裝巨舟，遣其屬善妙等四十餘人隨直等來貢市，於三十六年十月初，抵舟山之岑港。

translations.literal: They then fitted out great vessels and sent more than forty of their followers, including Zenmyō, to come with Zhi and the others to trade and pay tribute. In the tenth month of the thirty-sixth year they reached Cengang in Zhoushan.
translations.idiomatic: They fitted out large ships and sent more than forty men, including Zenmyō, to accompany Wang Zhi on a tribute-and-trade mission. In the tenth month of year thirty-six they reached Cengang in Zhoushan.

sentences.zh: 將吏以為入寇也，陳兵備。

translations.literal: The generals and officials thought this was an invasion and arrayed troops in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Local commanders took it for an attack and mobilized for defense.

sentences.zh: 直乃遣王？

translations.literal: Zhi then dispatched Wang Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi sent Wang Yao ahead.

sentences.zh: 滶入見宗憲，謂：「我以好來，何故陳兵待我？」

translations.literal: Ao entered to see Zongxian and said: "I have come in friendship — why do you array troops to receive me?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao went in to see Hu Zongxian and demanded: "I came in peace — why are your troops drawn up against me?

sentences.zh: 滶即毛海峰，直養子也。

translations.literal: Ao was Mao Haifeng, Zhi's adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: Ao was Mao Haifeng, Wang Zhi's adopted son.

sentences.zh: 宗憲慰勞甚至，指心誓無他。

translations.literal: Zongxian comforted and rewarded him to the utmost, pointed to his heart, and swore he had no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zongxian welcomed him lavishly, placed a hand on his heart, and swore he meant no treachery.

sentences.zh: 俄善妙等見副將盧鏜於舟山，鏜令擒直以獻。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zenmyō and the others met the vice general Lu Zong at Zhoushan, and Zong ordered that Zhi be seized and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zenmyō and the others met Vice General Lu Zong at Zhoushan, and Lu Zong ordered Wang Zhi seized and handed over.

sentences.zh: 語洩，直益疑。

translations.literal: The words leaked out, and Zhi's suspicions increased.
translations.idiomatic: Word of the order got out, and Wang Zhi's mistrust deepened.

sentences.zh: 宗憲開諭百方，直終不信，曰：「果爾，可遣滶出，吾當入見。」

translations.literal: Zongxian tried every means of persuasion, but Zhi ultimately did not believe him and said: "If that is truly so, send Ao out and I will come in to see you."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zongxian tried every argument, but Wang Zhi would not trust him. "If you mean no harm," he said, "send Ao back out and I will come ashore.

sentences.zh: 宗憲立遣之。

translations.literal: Zongxian immediately sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zongxian sent Ao out at once.

sentences.zh: 直又邀一貴官為質，即命指揮夏正往。

translations.literal: Zhi also demanded a high official as hostage, and Zongxian at once ordered the commander Xia Zheng to go.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi also demanded a senior officer as hostage, and Hu Zongxian sent Commander Xia Zheng.

sentences.zh: 直以為信，遂與宗滿、清溪偕來。

translations.literal: Zhi considered this trustworthy and then came together with Zongman and Qingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Taking this as proof of good faith, Wang Zhi came ashore with Ye Zongman and Wang Qingxi.

sentences.zh: 宗憲大喜，禮接之甚厚，令謁巡按御史王本固於杭州，本固以屬吏。

translations.literal: Zongxian rejoiced greatly, treated them with the utmost courtesy, and ordered them to pay their respects to the touring censor Wang Benguo at Hangzhou; Benguo treated them as subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zongxian was delighted, received them with great honor, and sent them to call on the touring censor Wang Benguo in Hangzhou, who treated them like ordinary prisoners.

sentences.zh: 滶等聞，大恨，支解夏正，焚舟登山，據岑港堅守。

translations.literal: When Ao and the others heard this, they hated it intensely; they dismembered Xia Zheng, burned their boats, ascended the hills, and held Cengang in a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ao and his men learned what had happened, they were furious. They killed Xia Zheng by dismemberment, burned their ships, took to the hills, and dug in at Cengang.

sentences.zh: 踰年，新倭大至，屢寇浙東三郡。

translations.literal: After more than a year, a great new force of Wo bandits arrived and repeatedly raided the three prefectures of eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later fresh Japanese raiders arrived in force and struck eastern Zhejiang's three prefectures again and again.

sentences.zh: 其在岑港者，徐移之柯梅，造新舟出海，宗憲不之追。

translations.literal: Those at Cengang gradually shifted to Keme, built new boats, and put out to sea; Zongxian did not pursue them.
translations.idiomatic: The men at Cengang slipped away to Keme, built new ships, and sailed off; Hu Zongxian did not chase them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，賊揚帆南去，泊泉州之浯嶼，掠同安、惠安、南安諸縣，攻福寧州，破福安、寧德。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the bandits set sail south, anchored at Wuyu in Quanzhou, plundered the counties of Tong'an, Hui'an, and Nan'an, attacked Funing Prefecture, and broke Fu'an and Ningde.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the pirates sailed south to Wuyu off Quanzhou, looted Tong'an, Hui'an, and Nan'an, attacked Funing Prefecture, and overran Fu'an and Ningde.

sentences.zh: 明年四月遂圍福州，經月不解。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year they then besieged Fuzhou and did not lift the siege for a month.
translations.idiomatic: The next April they besieged Fuzhou and held it under siege for a month.

sentences.zh: 福清、永福諸城皆被攻毀，蔓延於興化，奔突於漳州。

translations.literal: The cities of Fuqing and Yongfu were all attacked and destroyed; the calamity spread into Xinghua and surged into Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fuqing and Yongfu were battered and broken, the disaster spread into Xinghua, and raiders stampeded into Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其患盡移於福建，而潮、廣間亦紛紛以倭警聞矣。

translations.literal: The affliction had entirely shifted to Fujian, and reports of Wo alarms also came in one after another from the Chaozhou and Guangdong region.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis had moved wholesale to Fujian, and alarms of pirate raids began pouring in from Chaozhou and Guangdong as well.

sentences.zh: 至四十年，浙東、江北諸寇以次平。

translations.literal: By the fortieth year, the bandits in eastern Zhejiang and the north were pacified in succession.
translations.idiomatic: By year forty, pirates in eastern Zhejiang and the north had been subdued one after another.

sentences.zh: 宗憲尋坐罪被逮。

translations.literal: Before long Zongxian was implicated in a crime and arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hu Zongxian was implicated in misconduct and arrested.

sentences.zh: 明年十一月陷興化府，大殺掠，移據平海衛不去。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the following year they captured Xinghua Prefecture, slaughtered and plundered on a great scale, and moved to hold Pinghai Guard without leaving.
translations.idiomatic: The next November they took Xinghua Prefecture, massacred and looted the city, and settled in at Pinghai Guard.

sentences.zh: 初，倭之犯浙江也，破州縣衛所城以百數，然未有破府城者。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Wo invaded Zhejiang, they broke prefectures, counties, guard posts, and walled cities numbering in the hundreds, yet there had never been a case of breaking a prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier raids in Zhejiang had overrun hundreds of counties, guard posts, and walled towns, but no prefectural seat had fallen.

sentences.zh: 至是，遠近震動，亟征俞大猷、戚繼光、劉顯諸將合擊，破之。

translations.literal: At this the near and far were shaken; Yu Dayou, Qi Jiguang, Liu Xian, and other generals were urgently summoned for a joint attack, and the bandits were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The shock ran deep. Yu Dayou, Qi Jiguang, Liu Xian, and other generals were rushed to the scene, joined forces, and broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 其侵犯他州縣者，亦 為諸將所破，福建亦平。

translations.literal: Those who had invaded other prefectures and counties were also defeated by the various generals, and Fujian too was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Raids in other prefectures and counties were beaten back as well, and Fujian was finally pacified.

sentences.zh: 其後，廣東巨寇曾一本、黃朝太等，無不引倭為助。

translations.literal: Afterward, the great bandits of Guangdong such as Zeng Yiben and Huang Chaotai all, without exception, drew on Wo bandits for support.
translations.idiomatic: After that, major Guangdong outlaws such as Zeng Yiben and Huang Chaotai routinely enlisted Japanese raiders as allies.

sentences.zh: 隆慶時，破碣石、甲子諸衛所。

translations.literal: In the Longqing period they broke Jieshi, Jiazi, and other guard posts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign they overran Jieshi, Jiazi, and other guard posts.

sentences.zh: 已，犯化州石城縣，陷錦囊所、神電衛。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they invaded Shicheng County in Huazhou and captured Jinnang Post and Shendian Guard.
translations.idiomatic: They soon struck Shicheng County in Huazhou and took Jinnang Post and Shendian Guard.

sentences.zh: 吳川、陽江、茂名、海豐、新寧、惠來諸縣，悉遭焚掠。

translations.literal: The counties of Wuchuan, Yangjiang, Maoming, Haifeng, Xinning, and Huilai all suffered burning and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchuan, Yangjiang, Maoming, Haifeng, Xinning, and Huilai were all burned and looted.

sentences.zh: 轉入雷、謙、瓊三郡境，亦被其患。

translations.literal: Turning into the territories of the three prefectures of Lei, Lian, and Qiong, they also suffered from their affliction.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders pushed into Leizhou, Lianzhou, and Qiongzhou and brought the same devastation there.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年犯浙東寧、紹、台、溫四郡，又陷廣東銅鼓石雙魚所。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli they invaded the four prefectures of Ning, Shao, Tai, and Wen in eastern Zhejiang, and also captured the Tonggushi and Shuangyu posts in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 2 they hit Ningbo, Shaoxing, Taizhou, and Wenzhou in eastern Zhejiang and also took Guangdong's Tonggushi and Shuangyu posts.

sentences.zh: 三年犯電白。

translations.literal: In the third year they invaded Dianbai.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 3 they raided Dianbai.

sentences.zh: 四年犯定海。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they invaded Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 4 they struck Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 八年犯浙江韭山及福建彭湖、東涌。

translations.literal: In the eighth year they invaded Jiushan in Zhejiang and Penghu and Dongyong in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 8 they hit Jiushan in Zhejiang and Penghu and Dongyong in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 十年犯溫州，又犯廣東。

translations.literal: In the tenth year they invaded Wenzhou and also invaded Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 10 they raided Wenzhou and Guangdong again.

sentences.zh: 十六年犯浙江。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year they invaded Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 16 they struck Zhejiang once more.

sentences.zh: 然時疆吏懲嘉靖之禍，海防頗飭，賊來輒失利。

translations.literal: Yet by this time the frontier officials, chastened by the calamity of the Jiajing era, had fairly tightened sea defense, and whenever the bandits came they usually met with defeat.
translations.idiomatic: By then, however, frontier officials had learned from the Jiajing disasters and kept tighter coastal defenses, and raiders usually lost when they came.

sentences.zh: 其犯廣東者，為蜒賊梁本豪勾引，勢尤猖獗。

translations.literal: Those who invaded Guangdong were lured in by the pirate bandit Liang Benhao, and their force was especially rampant.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong raids were especially fierce because the pirate Liang Benhao was drawing them in.

sentences.zh: 總督陳瑞集眾軍擊之，斬首千六百餘級，沈其船百餘艘，本豪亦授首。

translations.literal: The governor-general Chen Rui assembled the armies and struck them, beheading more than sixteen hundred men, sinking more than a hundred of their boats, and Benhao too surrendered his head.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Chen Rui massed his forces, killed more than sixteen hundred enemies, sank over a hundred ships, and Liang Benhao lost his head as well.

sentences.zh: 帝為告謝郊廟，宣捷受賀雲。

translations.literal: The emperor for this reason reported thanks at the suburban altars and the ancestral temple and proclaimed the victory, receiving congratulations and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor offered thanks at the suburban altars and ancestral temple, proclaimed victory, and received the usual round of congratulations.

sentences.zh: 日本故有王，其下稱關白者最尊，時以山城州渠信長為之。

translations.literal: Japan originally had a king; below him the office called kampaku was the most honored, and at this time the chieftain of Yamashiro Province, Nobunaga, held it.
translations.idiomatic: Japan still had a king in name, but the highest real office was kampaku, held at the time by Oda Nobunaga of Yamashiro.

sentences.zh: 偶出獵，遇一人臥樹下，驚起衝突，執而詰之。

translations.literal: By chance, while out hunting, he came upon a man lying beneath a tree; startled, the man rose and collided with him, and Nobunaga seized and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Once while hunting, Nobunaga found a man asleep under a tree. The man started up and bumped into him, and Nobunaga seized and questioned him.

sentences.zh: 自言為平秀吉，薩摩州人之奴，雄健蹺捷，有口辯。

translations.literal: He said his name was Hideyoshi, a slave of a man from Satsuma Province; he was strong and nimble and had a gift for speech.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his name as Hideyoshi, a servant from Satsuma — strong, quick, and sharp-tongued.

sentences.zh: 信長悅之，令牧馬，名曰木下人。

translations.literal: Nobunaga was pleased with him, put him to tending horses, and called him "the man under the tree."
translations.idiomatic: Nobunaga took a liking to him, set him to mind horses, and nicknamed him "Under-the-Tree."

sentences.zh: 後漸用事，為信長畫策，奪並二十餘州，遂為攝津鎮守大將。

translations.literal: Later he gradually came to handle affairs, devised strategies for Nobunaga, seized and merged more than twenty provinces, and then became the great general guarding Settsu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in Nobunaga's service, planned campaigns that swallowed more than twenty provinces, and became military governor of Settsu.

sentences.zh: 有參謀阿奇支者，得罪信長，命秀吉統兵討之。

translations.literal: There was a staff officer named Akechi who offended Nobunaga, and Nobunaga ordered Hideyoshi to command troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When a staff officer named Akechi offended Nobunaga, Nobunaga sent Hideyoshi to crush him.

sentences.zh: 俄信長為其下明智所殺，秀吉方攻滅阿奇支，聞變，與部將行長等乘勝還兵誅之，威名益振。

translations.literal: Soon Nobunaga was killed by his subordinate Akechi. Hideyoshi was then attacking and destroying the Akechi faction; when he heard of the change, he returned with his generals Yukinaga and the others, took advantage of victory to march back and execute Akechi, and his fame shook the realm all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Nobunaga was murdered by his own man Akechi Mitsuhide. Hideyoshi was campaigning against Akechi's faction when news arrived; he wheeled about with generals such as Yukinaga, marched on the capital, destroyed Akechi, and his renown soared.

sentences.zh: 尋廢信長三子，僭稱關白，盡有其眾，時為萬曆十四年。

translations.literal: Before long he deposed Nobunaga's three sons, usurped the title of kampaku, and completely took over his following; this was in the fourteenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He soon displaced Nobunaga's three sons, seized the title of kampaku, and absorbed his armies — this was Wanli 14.

sentences.zh: 於是益治兵，征服六十六州，又以威脅琉球、呂宋、暹羅、佛郎機諸國，皆使奉貢。

translations.literal: Thereupon he further trained troops, conquered the sixty-six provinces, and by intimidation also compelled Ryukyu, Luzon, Siam, and the Franks to submit tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled his armies, unified the sixty-six provinces, and by force or fear made Ryukyu, Luzon, Siam, and the Portuguese pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 乃改國王所居山城為大閣，廣築 城郭，建宮殿，其樓閣有至九重者，實婦女珍寶其中。

translations.literal: He then renamed the Yamashiro where the king had dwelt as the Great Tower, extensively built city walls and ramparts, and erected palaces; some of the towered halls rose nine stories high, and he filled them with women and treasure.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed the Yamashiro capital the Great Tower, greatly expanded its walls and ramparts, and built palaces whose loftiest halls rose nine stories, stocked with women and treasure.

sentences.zh: 其用法嚴，軍行有進無退，違者雖子婿必誅，以故所向無敵。

translations.literal: His laws were strict; on campaign there was advance but no retreat, and even sons-in-law who violated orders were executed. For this reason, wherever he turned, none could withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: His discipline was brutal: armies moved forward, never back, and even a son-in-law who disobeyed was put to death. That was why his campaigns seemed unstoppable.

sentences.zh: 乃改元文祿，並欲侵中國，滅朝鮮而有之。

translations.literal: He then changed the era name to Bunroku and also intended to invade China and destroy Korea and possess it.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed the Bunroku era and set his sights on invading China, conquering Korea, and holding both.

sentences.zh: 召問故時汪直遺黨，知唐人畏倭如虎，氣益驕。

translations.literal: He summoned and questioned the old followers left by Wang Zhi, learned that the people of Tang feared the Wo like tigers, and his arrogance increased all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned Wang Zhi's old associates, heard that Chinese feared Japanese like tigers, and grew still more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 益大治兵甲，繕舟艦，與其下謀，入中國北京者用朝鮮人為導，入浙、閩沿海郡縣者用唐人為導。

translations.literal: He further greatly prepared armor and weapons, repaired boats and warships, and plotted with his subordinates: to enter Beijing in China they would use Koreans as guides; to enter the coastal prefectures and counties of Zhe and Min they would use men of Tang as guides.
translations.idiomatic: He doubled down on arms and shipbuilding and planned with his commanders to use Koreans as guides for an advance on Beijing and Chinese collaborators for the coasts of Zhejiang and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 慮琉球洩其情，使毋入貢。

translations.literal: Fearing that Ryukyu would leak his plans, he ordered it not to send tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid Ryukyu would expose his plans, he blocked its tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 同安人陳甲者，商於琉球。

translations.literal: A man of Tong'an named Chen Jia traded in Ryukyu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jia of Tong'an was a merchant in Ryukyu.

sentences.zh: 懼為中國害，與琉球長史鄭迥謀，因進貢請封之使，具以其情來告。

translations.literal: Fearing harm to China, he plotted with the chief secretary of Ryukyu, Zheng Jiong, and through the tribute mission requesting investiture had an envoy fully report their situation.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing disaster for the Ming, he worked with Ryukyu's chief secretary Zheng Jiong to slip word to Beijing through the next investiture tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 甲又旋故鄉，陳其事於巡撫趙參魯。

translations.literal: Jia also returned to his native place and reported the matter to the grand coordinator Zhao Canlu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jia went home as well and told Grand Coordinator Zhao Canlu what he knew.

sentences.zh: 參魯以聞，下兵部，部移咨朝鮮王。

translations.literal: Canlu reported it upward; the matter was sent down to the Ministry of War, and the ministry sent a dispatch to the king of Korea.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Canlu forwarded the report to the Ministry of War, which in turn notified the Korean king.

sentences.zh: 王但深辨嚮導之誣，亦不知其謀己也。

translations.literal: The king only argued at length that the charge of serving as guides was slander, and he too did not know that Hideyoshi was plotting against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Korean king insisted the guide story was slander — and had no idea Hideyoshi was plotting against him.

sentences.zh: 初，秀吉廣徵諸鎮兵，諸三歲糧，欲自將以犯中國。

translations.literal: Initially, Hideyoshi broadly conscripted troops from the various domains and three years' worth of grain, intending to lead them in person to invade China.
translations.idiomatic: Hideyoshi had begun mass conscription across the domains, stockpiling three years of grain for a personal invasion of China.

sentences.zh: 會其子死，旁無兄弟。

translations.literal: Then his son died, and he had no brothers at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Then his heir died, leaving him without a brother at hand.

sentences.zh: 前奪豐後島主妻為妾，慮其為後患。

translations.literal: He had earlier taken the wife of the lord of Bungo Island as a concubine and feared she would become a source of future trouble.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier taken the Bungo lord's wife as a concubine and now worried she would become a liability.

sentences.zh: 而諸鎮怨秀吉暴虐，咸曰：「此舉非襲大唐，乃襲我耳。」

translations.literal: But the various domains resented Hideyoshi's cruelty and tyranny, all saying: This campaign is not aimed at the Great Tang—it is aimed at us.
translations.idiomatic: The daimyo resented Hideyoshi's cruelty and tyranny, saying among themselves: This war is not against China—it is against us.

sentences.zh: 各懷異志。

translations.literal: Each harbored divergent intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Each harbored his own private designs.

sentences.zh: 由是，秀吉不敢親行。

translations.literal: Because of this, Hideyoshi did not dare to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Hideyoshi did not dare lead the expedition himself.

sentences.zh: 二十年四月遣其將清正、行長、義智，僧玄蘇、宗逸等，將舟師數百艘，由對馬島渡海陷朝鮮之釜山，乘勝長驅，以五月渡臨津，掠開城，分陷豐德諸郡。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Wanli, the fourth month, he sent his generals Kiyomasa, Teruzumi, and Yoshitoshi, together with the monks Genso and Soitsu and others, with several hundred warships crossing the sea from Tsushima Island to take Korea's Pusan, then pressing on in victory—in the fifth month crossing the Imjin, plundering Kaesong, and separately falling on the various districts of Pungdok.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Wanli 20 he sent his generals Kiyomasa, Teruzumi, and Yoshitoshi, with the monks Genso and Soitsu, leading several hundred warships from Tsushima. They crossed the sea, took Pusan, swept forward in victory, crossed the Imjin in the fifth month, seized Kaesong, and overran the districts of Pungdok.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮望風潰，清正等遂亻畐王京。

translations.literal: Korea collapsed wherever the wind blew; Kiyomasa and the others then pressed on the royal capital.
translations.idiomatic: Korean armies collapsed without a fight. Kiyomasa and the others then pressed on the royal capital.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮王李昖棄城奔平壤，又奔義州，遣使絡繹告急。

translations.literal: King Yi Sun of Korea abandoned the city and fled to Pyongyang, then fled again to Uiju, sending envoys in unbroken succession to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: King Yi Sun abandoned the capital and fled to Pyongyang, then to Uiju, sending envoys in rapid succession to beg for aid.

sentences.zh: 倭遂入王京，執其王妃、王子，追奔至平壤，放兵淫掠。

translations.literal: The Wo then entered the royal capital, seized the queen consort and princes, pursued the flight as far as Pyongyang, and let their troops run wild in rape and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese entered the capital, seized the queen and princes, pursued the king to Pyongyang, and let their troops ravage the countryside.

sentences.zh: 七月命副總兵祖承訓赴援，與倭戰於平壤城外，大敗，承訓僅以身免。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he ordered Vice Commander-in-Chief Zu Chengxun to go to the rescue; he fought the Wo outside Pyongyang and suffered a great defeat—Chengxun barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Vice Commander Zu Chengxun was sent to relieve Korea. He fought the Japanese outside Pyongyang, suffered a crushing defeat, and barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 八月，中朝乃以兵部侍郎宋應昌為經略，都督李如松為提督，統兵討之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the central court appointed Vice Minister of War Song Yingchang as supreme coordinator and Censor-in-Chief Li Rusong as commander-in-chief to lead troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the court appointed Vice Minister Song Yingchang as supreme coordinator and Li Rusong as commander-in-chief to lead the punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 當是時，寧夏未平，朝鮮事起，兵部尚書石星計無所出，募能說倭者偵之，於是嘉興人沈惟敬應募。

translations.literal: At that time Ningxia was not yet pacified and the Korean crisis had erupted; War Minister Shi Xing could find no plan, so he recruited anyone who could negotiate with the Wo to spy on them—thereupon Shen Weijing of Jiaxing answered the call.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia was still unsettled when the Korean war broke out. War Minister Shi Xing, at his wits' end, recruited anyone who claimed he could deal with Japan. Shen Weijing of Jiaxing volunteered.

sentences.zh: 星即假游擊將軍銜，送之如松麾下。

translations.literal: Xing at once gave him the titular rank of mobile corps commander and sent him under Li Rusong's command.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xing gave him the titular rank of mobile corps commander and attached him to Li Rusong's staff.

sentences.zh: 明年，如松師大捷於平壤，朝鮮所失四道並復。

translations.literal: The next year Li Rusong's army won a great victory at Pyongyang, and the four lost Korean provinces were all recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Li Rusong won a great victory at Pyongyang and recovered all four lost Korean provinces.

sentences.zh: 如松乘勝趨碧蹄館，敗而退師。

translations.literal: Li Rusong pressed the advantage toward Pyeongjeck, was defeated, and withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rusong pressed on to Pyeongjeck, was defeated, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是封貢之議起，中朝彌縫惟敬以成款局，事詳《朝鮮傳》。

translations.literal: Thereupon the debate over investiture and tribute arose; the central court patched matters up through Weijing to conclude a truce—the details are given in the Korea biography.
translations.idiomatic: Talk of investiture and tribute followed, and the court patched peace together through Shen Weijing. The affair is detailed in the Korea biography.

sentences.zh: 久之，秀吉死，諸倭揚帆盡歸，朝鮮患亦平。

translations.literal: After a long time Hideyoshi died; the various Wo raised sail and all returned, and Korea's calamity was also pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Hideyoshi died. The Japanese fleets sailed home, and Korea's ordeal ended.

sentences.zh: 然自關白侵東國，前後七載，喪師數十萬糜餉數百萬，中朝與朝鮮迄無勝算。

translations.literal: Yet from the kampaku's invasion of the eastern state, for seven years in all, armies in the hundreds of thousands were lost and supplies in the millions squandered—neither the central court nor Korea ever gained a decisive victory.
translations.idiomatic: Yet over seven years of Hideyoshi's invasion, hundreds of thousands of soldiers perished and millions in supplies were wasted, and neither Ming nor Korea ever achieved a decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 至關白死，兵禍始休，諸倭亦皆退守島巢，東南稍有安枕之日矣。

translations.literal: Only when the kampaku died did the military disaster cease; the various Wo also all withdrew to their island lairs, and the southeast at last had days of sleeping on a pillow in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Only with Hideyoshi's death did the war end. The Japanese withdrew to their islands, and the southeast coast at last knew a measure of peace.

sentences.zh: 秀吉凡再傳而亡。

translations.literal: Hideyoshi passed through two more successions and then perished.
translations.idiomatic: Hideyoshi's line survived two more generations and then died out.

sentences.zh: 終明之世，通倭之禁甚嚴，閭巷小民，至指倭相詈罵，甚以噤其小兒女雲。

translations.literal: Through the entire Ming dynasty the prohibition on communicating with Japan was very strict; even common people in the lanes would point at someone and curse him as a Wo, and even used the name to frighten their little children.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Ming dynasty the ban on contact with Japan was severe. Neighbors would curse one another as 'Japanese,' and parents even used the word to frighten small children.
